  • Troubleshooting income tax

docs.title: Generate Annual Summary Model 190 in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The model 190 is the annual declaration that summarizes all income tax withholdings during the fiscal year, detailing information per payee. It is mandatory for any company that has applied withholdings and must be filed electronically.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• All payrolls for the fiscal year are calculated
  • All income tax journal entries for the year are posted
  • Periodic settlements for the year are completed
  • Employee IRPF data is updated (perception keys, sub-keys)

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Liquidaciones IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. Choose the Model 190 action to generate the electronic file in AEAT format.
  3. The system processes all income tax payees for the fiscal year
  4. It generates type 1 records (declarant), type 2 records (payees), and type 3 records (totals)
  5. The file includes: perception key/sub-key, cash and in-kind amounts, withholdings, payments on account
  6. To obtain the printed verification report: run the IRPF 190 Summary report.
  7. Groups data by perception key
  8. Shows subtotals per key
  9. Allows verification before submission

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The electronic file is generated according to AEAT specifications. The printed report grouped by perception key is available for verification before filing.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Generate periodic settlement model 111
  • Generate non-resident settlements models 216 and 296
  • Cancel an income tax settlement

docs.title: Generate Non-Resident Settlements Models 216 and 296 in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Companies with non-resident payees must file model 216 (quarterly) with the withholdings applied, and model 296 (annual) as a summary. Both have specific electronic file formats.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Non-resident payees registered with specific non-resident perception keys
  • Withholdings applied during the period or fiscal year

docs.title: Generate quarterly model 216
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Liquidaciones IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. Choose the Model 216 action to generate the quarterly electronic file.
  3. Select the year and quarter.

docs.title: Generate annual model 296
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Liquidaciones IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. Choose the Model 296 action at the end of the fiscal year.
  3. The system processes payees with non-resident perception keys
  4. It generates the file according to the HAC/2116/2003 regulation

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The electronic file for model 216 or 296 is generated in the corresponding folder configured in the tax administration.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Generate periodic settlement model 111
  • Generate annual summary model 190

docs.title: Generate Periodic Settlement Model 111 in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Each fiscal period (monthly for model 111 in large companies, quarterly for model 111T in SMEs) you must generate the settlement that totals withholdings and enables electronic submission to the tax authority (AEAT).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Payrolls for the period are calculated with income tax withholdings
  • Income tax journal entries for the period are posted (if any)
  • Settlement folders configured in the tax administration

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Liquidaciones IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. Choose the settlement calculation action for model 111 (or 111T).
  3. Select:
  4. Year: The fiscal year (for example, 2025)
  5. Period: The month or quarter code (for example, 03 for March)
  6. Tax Administration Code: The corresponding administration
  7. The system generates the settlement record with totals:
  8. Cash work income (number of payees, amounts, withholdings)
  9. In-kind work income
  10. Professional activity income
  11. Verify the totals in the settlements list.
  12. To generate the electronic file: choose the Model 111 (or Model 111T) action from the settlements list.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A settlement record is created in the list with all amounts broken down by income type. The electronic file is generated in the folder configured in the tax administration. The file name follows the format: TAXID_YY_MM.111.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Cancel an income tax settlement
  • Generate annual summary model 190
  • Troubleshooting income tax

docs.title: Import Income Tax Entries from Excel in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When you have a high volume of external income tax movements (professional invoices, bulk adjustments, historical data migration), it is more efficient to import them from an Excel file than to enter them manually in the journal.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An Excel file with the required columns: employee code, period, amount, retention, perception key
  • All referenced employees must exist in the system

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Prepare the Excel file with the required columns.
  2. Choose the search icon, enter "Diario IRPF", and choose the related link.
  3. Choose the import from Excel action.
  4. Select the Excel file using the file selection dialog.
  5. Specify the sheet name from the Excel workbook.
  6. The system imports the lines and creates them in the journal.
  7. Review the imported lines.
  8. Choose the Post action to process the movements.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The Excel lines are created as income tax journal lines. After posting, payroll headers of type IRPF are generated. The movements appear in the settlement for the corresponding period.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Register income tax journal entries
  • Generate periodic settlement model 111

docs.title: Recalculate Withholding for Specific Employees in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When you detect an error in a specific employee's calculation or their personal circumstances change mid-year, you can recalculate only the affected employees without altering the rest of the proposals.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Form 145 data corrected for the affected employees
  • An existing percentage change proposal in the journal (generated with "Calculate proposal")

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Cambios % Reten.IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by the affected employee using the Employee No. field.
  3. Choose the Recalculate proposal action.
  4. The system recalculates the proposed percentage for the filtered lines only, leaving the rest unchanged.
  5. Verify the new Proposed % and Variation.
  6. If correct, mark the line and choose Change marked.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Only the filtered employees have their proposal updated. Unfiltered lines remain unchanged. The updated percentage is applied to the employee's record.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Calculate withholding percentage proposals
  • Register Form 145 data for an employee

docs.title: Register Form 145 Data for an Employee in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee communicates changes in their personal or family situation (new child, marital status change, recognized disability, mortgage), you must record this data so the income tax calculation is correct.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Signed Form 145 document from the employee
  • The employee must already exist in the system

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Inform. IRPF Perceptores", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the employee in the list.
  3. Open the card by selecting the line.
  4. Create a new communication (new line with Last communication = current date).
  5. Fill in the fields:
  6. Family situation: Select the appropriate status (Not married with children, With dependent spouse, Without dependent spouse)
  7. Spouse NIF: If status is "With dependent spouse"
  8. Number of children: Count of dependents
  9. Disability percentage: If applicable
  10. Disability degree: Filled automatically based on percentage
  11. Housing mortgage: If the employee has a pre-2011 mortgage deduction
  12. Post-2011 mortgage: If the mortgage was constituted after 2011
  13. Save the card.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The communication is recorded with the date. The system uses this data in the next withholding percentage calculation. You should recalculate the employee's withholding percentage so the new rate reflects the communicated data.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Recalculate withholding for specific employees
  • Calculate withholding percentage proposals

docs.title: Register Income Tax Journal Entries in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The income tax journal is used to record withholding movements that do not come from standard payroll calculation: professional invoices, adjustments, or manual corrections. These movements generate payroll headers of type IRPF and are included in periodic settlements.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee (payee) exists in the system
  • You have the retention details: base amount, withholding percentage, and period

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Diario IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. Create a new line in the journal:
  3. Employee No.: Enter the payee code
  4. Period: Date of the retention period
  5. Employee key: Key assigned to the payee
  6. Perception key: Fiscal perception key (for example, professional)
  7. Withholding %: The retention percentage
  8. Amount: Base amount subject to withholding
  9. Retention: Withheld amount (calculated as Amount x Withholding %)
  10. Social security quota: If applicable
  11. Review the line data.
  12. Choose the Post action.
  13. Confirm when the system asks to post the income tax journal.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system creates a payroll header of type IRPF with remuneration and deduction lines. The processed lines are removed from the journal. The movements appear in the settlement for the corresponding period.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Import income tax entries from Excel
  • Generate periodic settlement model 111

docs.title: Set Up Income Tax Withholding for a Fiscal Year in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: At the beginning of each fiscal year, you must configure the income tax parameters with the latest regulatory values published in the official gazette. This ensures that withholding percentage calculations are accurate for the new year.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Company configured with IRPF = Yes in company setup
  • At least one tax administration created (State or Regional)
  • Perception keys configured with fiscal treatment assigned
  • Employees registered with social security units and work centers

docs.title: Step 1: Configure IRPF parameters for the fiscal year
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Configuracion IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. Set the Year field to the current fiscal year.
  3. Configure special percentages:
  4. Administrators and board members %: Fixed withholding percentage for administration roles
  5. Professional income %: Withholding percentage for professional activities
  6. Arrears %: Percentage for previous year arrears
  7. Minimum % contracts < 1 year: Minimum for temporary contracts
  8. Minimum % special relationships: Minimum for special labor relationships
  9. Configure work income reductions (limits and amounts for the four brackets).
  10. Configure personal and family minimums:
  11. General personal minimum, increase for over 65
  12. Disability minimums (33-65% and >65%)
  13. Dependents minimums (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th+ child)
  14. Children under 3, children with disability
  15. Ascendants minimums (>65, >75, with disability)
  16. Configure family situation thresholds (exemption limits by marital status and children).

docs.title: Step 2: Load retention tables
docs.text:
The retention tables contain the progressive tax brackets.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Tabla retenc. IRPF", and choose the related link.
  2. For each tax bracket, create a line with:
  3. Year: Fiscal year
  4. Regional tax authority: State or the corresponding regional territory
  5. Income amount: Lower limit of the bracket
  6. Retention quota: Fixed quota for the bracket
  7. % Remainder: Marginal percentage for the excess
  8. Children 0 to 11+: Percentage by number of children (for alternative calculation)

If your company operates in a regional tax territory, load brackets for both the state regime and each applicable regional authority.

docs.title: Step 3: Verify Form 145 data for employees
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Inform. IRPF Perceptores", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that each active employee has at least one communication recorded with:
  3. Family situation: filled in
  4. Number of children: correct count
  5. Spouse NIF: if status is "With dependent spouse"
  6. Disability degree: if applicable
  7. Mortgage: if applicable

docs.title: Step 4: Verify the tax administration
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Administraciones Hacienda", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify each administration has:
  3. Monthly settlement folder: Path for model 111 files
  4. Quarterly settlement folder: Path for model 111T files
  5. Tax domicile: Required for electronic file generation

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The income tax module is ready for the new fiscal year. You can now calculate withholding percentage proposals for employees.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Calculate withholding percentage proposals
  • Register Form 145 data for an employee

docs.title: Troubleshooting Income Tax Issues in Omne RH Payroll
Error when choosing "Change all" or "Change marked"
docs.text:
Symptom: The system shows an error and does not apply any changes.

Cause: The system requires the cursor to be on a line with the Year field filled in.

Solution: Position the cursor on any line that has the Year field filled and choose the action again.

docs.title: Proposed percentage is 0% for an employee with salary
docs.text:
Symptom: After choosing "Calculate proposal", some employees show proposed % = 0.

Cause: One of the following:

  • The employee's net income (after reductions and minimums) is below the taxable minimum
  • Form 145 data is not filled in, resulting in no applicable reductions
  • Retention tables for the year and corresponding tax authority are not loaded

Solution:

  1. If salary is low: this is a correct result (exempt from withholding).
  2. If Form 145 data is missing: fill it in and recalculate.
  3. If retention tables are not loaded: load them before recalculating.

docs.title: Cannot generate the electronic file for model 111
docs.text:
Symptom: When trying to generate the electronic file, the system shows an error.

Cause: The tax administration does not have the tax domicile configured, which is required for electronic file generation.

Solution:

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Administraciones Hacienda", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the corresponding administration.
  3. Fill in the tax domicile field.
  4. Verify the settlement folders (monthly and/or quarterly).
  5. Try generating the file again.

docs.title: Unexpected confirmation when changing percentage for an employee with fixed rate
docs.text:
Symptom: When applying "Change all" or "Change marked", the system shows a confirmation dialog for certain employees.

Cause: The employee has a fixed percentage requested via Form 145. The system asks for confirmation because there is a discrepancy between the fixed and proposed rates.

Solution: Respond to the dialog based on your criteria:

  • Yes: The percentage changes and the fixed mark is removed.
  • No: The current fixed percentage is maintained.

docs.title: Cannot mark both pre-2011 and post-2011 mortgage simultaneously
docs.text:
Symptom: When trying to mark one mortgage option while the other is already marked, the system shows an error.

Cause: Both fields are mutually exclusive. Tax regulations distinguish between mortgages constituted before and after 2011 with different deduction regimes.

Solution: Unmark one field before marking the other. Select the one that corresponds to the actual mortgage constitution date.

docs.title: NIF validation error when registering Form 145 data
docs.text:
Symptom: When entering the spouse NIF or employee document, the system shows a validation error.

Cause: The NIF format is incorrect or the control letter is invalid.

Solution: Enter the NIF in the correct format: 8 digits + control letter (for example, 12345678Z). For NIE: initial letter (X/Y/Z) + 7 digits + control letter.

docs.title: Settlement duplicates amounts when regenerating
docs.text:
Symptom: After regenerating a settlement for the same period, amounts appear doubled.

Cause: The settlement calculation was run without first canceling the previous settlement for the same period.

Solution:

  1. Cancel the duplicate settlement.
  2. Verify that only one correct settlement remains for the period.
  3. If needed, cancel all settlements for the period and regenerate once.

docs.title: Employees missing from model 190 annual summary
docs.text:
Symptom: When generating model 190, the file does not contain some employee records.

Cause: One of the following:

  • Payrolls were not calculated for all months of the fiscal year
  • Income tax journal entries were not posted (still in draft)
  • Employees have incorrect or empty perception keys

Solution:

  1. Calculate any pending payrolls.
  2. Post pending income tax journal entries.
  3. Verify and correct perception keys in the IRPF employee table.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Calculate withholding percentage proposals
  • Set up income tax for a fiscal year
  • Cancel an income tax settlement

docs.title: Labor Agreements Overview in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The Labor Agreements module centralizes collective bargaining conditions: salary tables, professional categories, seniority brackets, and periodic revisions. When you apply an agreement, the system updates the perception schemes of all affected employees in bulk, respecting individual voluntary improvements.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• Labor agreement: A collective accord that defines compensation conditions for a group of workers. It contains one or more salary tables with effective dates.
  • Professional category: A job classification within an agreement that determines salary level, social security contribution group, and optional seniority or improvement groups.
  • Salary level: Groups categories that share the same salary amounts, so you define one line per concept instead of one per category.
  • Multi-validity: A single agreement can hold multiple effective dates (one per annual revision), preserving full history.
  • Agreement change flag: A flag on perception scheme lines that controls whether the line updates when you apply the agreement. Disabled lines are protected as voluntary improvements.
  • Part-time factor: When an employee contract has fewer hours than the agreement, amounts adjust proportionally: Contract hours / Agreement hours.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Create and maintain labor agreements with full salary tables.
  • Replicate salary tables applying a percentage increase for annual revisions.
  • Apply agreement conditions to employee perception schemes in bulk.
  • Protect individual salary improvements from being overwritten.
  • Navigate between multiple effective dates to view historical salary tables.
  • Import agreements from external NVN files.
  • Manage seniority complements by agreement or category.

docs.title: Shared data
docs.text: Labor agreements and professional categories are shared across all companies in Business Central. A change to an agreement affects every company that uses it.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Set Up Labor Agreements
  • Create a Labor Agreement
  • Replicate a Salary Table
  • Apply Agreement to Employees

docs.title: Apply a Labor Agreement to Employees in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The Apply action transfers the salary table from the agreement to the perception schemes of all employees assigned to that agreement. This is the key operation that connects collective conditions with each worker's individual payroll.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The agreement has a salary table for the active application date.
  • Employees are registered with the agreement and category assigned.
  • Perception schemes exist for the employees.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Labor Agreements", and choose the related link.
  2. Open the agreement card.
  3. Verify that the Application Date corresponds to the salary table you want to apply.
  4. Choose the Apply action (in the Process group).
  5. In the parameter window, optionally filter by category or employee range.
  6. Confirm the execution.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The system processes each employee assigned to the agreement:

  • For each salary table line:
  • If the concept already exists in the scheme with the Agreement Change flag active, the system updates the amount.
  • If the concept does not exist, the system inserts it into the scheme.
  • If the concept exists with the Agreement Change flag disabled, the system does not modify it (protected improvement).
  • Amounts are adjusted by the part-time factor if the employee's contract hours differ from the agreement hours.

docs.title: Part-time adjustment
docs.text:
The part-time factor is calculated as:

Contract weekly hours / Agreement weekly hours

This factor is applied automatically to all amounts for part-time employees.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Perception schemes of affected employees reflect the updated agreement amounts.
  • Lines with the Agreement Change flag disabled retain their original amounts.
  • Part-time employees have proportionally adjusted amounts.

  • Replicate a Salary Table
  • Navigate Agreement Dates

docs.title: Create a Labor Agreement in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Create a labor agreement to define the collective compensation conditions that will be applied to employees assigned to it.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Salary concepts are defined in the salary concepts master.
  • Professional categories are created with a contribution group assigned.
  • You know the agreement publication data (official gazette number, validity dates).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Labor Agreements", and choose the related link.
  2. Select New to create a new agreement card.
  3. In the Code field, enter a unique identifier (for example, METAL-BCN).
  4. In the Application Date field, enter the start date of the first salary table.
  5. Fill in the Description, Social Security Code, Weekly Hours, and Annual Hours fields.
  6. In the Validity section, fill in the Official Gazette No., Publication Date, In Force From, and In Force Until fields.
  7. Mark the territorial scope: State, Provincial, or Autonomous Community as applicable.
  8. In the Terms section, fill in Vacation Days and Vacation Day Type (Natural or Working days).
  9. In the Configuration section, select the Extra Pay Calculation method and configure the guaranteed salary flags as needed.
  10. In the lines subpage, create one line for each category and salary concept combination:
    • Select Category (or leave blank to apply by salary level).
    • Select Salary Concept. The system automatically inherits 13 fields from the concept master.
    • Enter the Amount or the Calculation Formula.
  11. Repeat for all categories and concepts in the agreement.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The agreement card shows all sections filled in, and the salary table lines appear in the lower subpage. The agreement is ready to be assigned to employees.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• Amount vs. Coefficient: These are mutually exclusive. If you enter a coefficient, the amount must be zero. Additionally, coefficients require a category to be specified on the line.
  • Calculation formula: Uses tokens representing salary concept codes (resolved to the concept amount in the scheme) and #1 for the annual working hours from Payroll Config.
  • Application date required: You cannot insert a line without first setting the application date in the header.

docs.text:
• Set Up Labor Agreements
  • Replicate a Salary Table
  • Apply Agreement to Employees

docs.title: Labor Agreements FAQ in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Answers to common questions about working with labor agreements in Omne RH Payroll.

docs.title: What happens to voluntary improvements when I apply a revision?
docs.text: If the perception scheme line has the Agreement Change flag disabled, the system respects it and does not overwrite it. If the flag is active, the amount updates to the agreement value and the improvement is lost. Always verify the flag before each bulk application.

docs.title: What is the difference between Category and Salary Level in agreement lines?
docs.text:
• With Category: The line applies exclusively to that specific professional category.
  • Without Category (by Salary Level): The line applies to all categories that share that salary level.

When applying the agreement, the system processes category-level lines first (high priority) and salary-level lines second (low priority). If a concept is defined in both, the category-level line takes precedence.

docs.title: How is the part-time factor calculated?
docs.text:
The factor is: Contract weekly hours / Agreement weekly hours.

It applies automatically when transferring the salary table to the perception scheme of an employee whose contract has fewer hours than the agreement. If either hours value is zero, the factor is not applied, which may produce incorrect results.

docs.title: Can I use formulas and fixed amounts in the same agreement?
docs.text:
Yes. Each line uses one of three mutually exclusive valuation methods:

Method When to use Amount For concepts with a known fixed value (base salary, fixed bonuses) Calculation formula For concepts whose amount depends on other concepts or on annual working hours Coefficient For concepts whose amount is a factor over another value (requires a category)

Formulas use tokens: salary concept codes (resolved to the concept amount in the scheme) and #1 (annual working hours from Payroll Config).

docs.title: Can I undo a replication with the wrong factor?
docs.text:
There is no automatic undo. Your options are:

  1. Manually delete the lines of the new application date and replicate again with the correct factor.
  2. Replicate again from the original table with the correct factor (creates another date).
  3. Manually modify the amounts in the replicated table.

The original salary table is never affected by replication.

docs.title: How do guaranteed salary parameters interact between agreement and company config?
docs.text: The hierarchy is: Agreement overrides Company Configuration. The guaranteed salary IT and AT fields in the agreement override the Company Configuration defaults for employees assigned to that agreement.

docs.title: Why do lines disappear when I change the application date?
docs.text: The agreement card works as a multi-validity document. The lines subpage only shows data for the selected application date. Changing the date navigates between different salary tables. If the selected date has no lines, the subpage appears empty. Use the Agreement Dates action to see which dates have salary tables.

docs.title: Blocked category vs. deleting a category: when to use each?
docs.text: Action Effect When to use Blocked = Yes The category does not appear in lookups but continues to exist. Historical employee records keep their reference When the category should not be assigned to new employees but historical records reference it Delete Permanently removed. Fails if records reference it Only if no record (employee, agreement line, historical entry) uses it

docs.title: Import a Labor Agreement from File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Import labor agreement definitions from external files in NVN format. The process reads two files: CABCON.NVN (header) and LINCON.NVN (lines), and creates or updates the agreement records.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• You have the CABCON.NVN and LINCON.NVN files in a compatible format.
  • The salary concepts referenced in the line file must already exist in the system.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Import Agreement", and choose the related link.
  2. Select the CABCON.NVN and LINCON.NVN files.
  3. Run the process.
  4. The system inserts or updates the agreement records and their lines.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• The imported agreements appear in the labor agreements list.
  • Salary lines are correctly associated to each agreement and application date.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• If the file references salary concepts that do not exist in the system, the import will fail for those lines. Create the missing concepts before importing.
  • If the agreement already exists with the same application date, review whether you want to update or keep the existing version.

docs.title: Manage Seniority by Agreement in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The system automatically calculates seniority complements for each employee based on seniority bracket tables. Brackets are defined by seniority group and can be linked to a specific agreement or be generic.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A seniority group is defined.
  • Seniority brackets are configured with concept, amount, and calculation key.
  • The agreement has a seniority group assigned (in the header or by category).
  • Employees have a seniority date informed.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Seniority Groups", and choose the related link.
  2. Create or verify the seniority group for the agreement.
  3. Define the brackets with the salary concept, bracket threshold, and amount for each tier (for example, 50 at 3 years, 100 at 6 years, 150 at 9 years).
  4. Open the labor agreement card.
  5. In the Seniority Group field, assign the corresponding group.
  6. If a specific category should use a different group, fill in the Seniority Group field on that professional category.

docs.title: How precedence works
docs.text:
The system determines which seniority group applies using this priority:

  1. If the professional category has a seniority group assigned, that group is used.
  2. If not, the agreement's seniority group is used.
  3. If neither has a group, no seniority complement is applied.

Within the selected group, the system checks:

  1. Brackets linked to the specific agreement take priority.
  2. If none exist, generic brackets (not linked to any agreement) are used.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The payroll engine automatically applies the appropriate seniority bracket based on the employee's tenure. The amount is included in the payroll calculation.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Create a Labor Agreement
  • Set Up Labor Agreements
  • Labor Agreements Overview

docs.title: Navigate Agreement Dates in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: A labor agreement can accumulate multiple application dates over its lifetime (one per salary revision). The agreement card only shows the lines for the currently selected application date. Use navigation actions to move between different historical salary tables.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • The agreement has at least two application dates (after a replication or manual creation).

docs.title: View all available dates
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Labor Agreements", and choose the related link.
  2. Open the agreement card.
  3. Choose the Agreement Dates action (in the Navigate group).
  4. The system shows a list of all application dates with their lines.

docs.title: Jump to the most recent salary table
docs.text:
1. Open the agreement card.
  2. Choose the Last Agreement Date action (in the Navigate group).
  3. The card repositions to show the most recent salary table.

docs.title: View a specific date
docs.text:
1. Open the agreement card.
  2. Change the Application Date field in the header to the desired date.
  3. The lines subpage updates to show the salary table for that date.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The lines in the subpage update to show the salary table corresponding to the selected date. Changing the date does not modify any data; it only changes the view.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• If the selected date has no lines defined, the subpage appears empty. This is normal for a newly created date that has not been replicated yet.
  • The original salary tables are never modified when you navigate between dates.

docs.text:

  • Create a Labor Agreement
  • Labor Agreements Overview

docs.title: Protect Voluntary Improvements in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee has an individual compensation condition that exceeds the agreement amount (voluntary improvement or ad personam), you can protect that line so future agreement applications do not overwrite it.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee has a perception scheme containing lines from the agreement.
  • You have identified the line or lines that represent the voluntary improvement.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the perception scheme for the employee.
  2. Locate the line for the concept you want to protect (for example, a productivity bonus).
  3. Toggle the Agreement Change flag:
  4. Disabled (false): The line is protected. It will not be modified in future agreement applications.
  5. Enabled (true): The line will be updated with the agreement amount on the next application.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Protected lines retain their individual amount after successive agreement applications.
  • Unprotected lines update normally with the agreement values.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• The Agreement Change flag is enabled by default when lines are inserted from the agreement. You must manually disable it for lines you want to protect.
  • If a protected line was accidentally overwritten (because the flag was active), restore the amount manually and disable the flag before the next application.
  • Review protected lines before each bulk application to ensure they are still correctly configured.

docs.text:
• Apply Agreement to Employees
  • Labor Agreements Overview

docs.title: Replicate a Salary Table in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a salary revision is published (typically annual), use the Replicate action to generate a new salary table with updated amounts based on a percentage increase.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The labor agreement has an existing salary table (at least one application date with lines).
  • You know the agreed salary increase percentage.
  • You know the new effective date.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Labor Agreements", and choose the related link.
  2. Open the agreement card to replicate (for example, METAL-BCN).
  3. Verify that the Application Date shown corresponds to the salary table you want to use as a base.
  4. Choose the Replicate action (in the Process group).
  5. In the parameter window:
  6. New Application Date: Enter the start date of the new table (for example, 01/01/2026).
  7. Factor: Enter the multiplier (for example, 1.03 for a 3% increase).
  8. Confirm the execution.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• A new application date appears in the agreement.
  • The lines contain the previous table amounts multiplied by the factor and rounded.
  • The original table remains intact as history.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• If you enter a factor of 1.00, the new table will have identical amounts to the original.
  • If you replicate with an incorrect factor, there is no automatic undo. You can delete the new date's lines and replicate again, or manually adjust the amounts.
  • The previous salary table is never modified by the replication process.

  • Navigate Agreement Dates
  • Create a Labor Agreement

docs.title: Create professional categories
docs.text:
Professional categories classify job positions within an agreement and determine the salary amounts that apply.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Professional Categories", and choose the related link.

  4. Code: A unique identifier for the category (for example, ADMIN).
  5. Description: A descriptive name (for example, Administrative).

  7. Salary Level: A code to group categories that share the same salary amounts.
  8. Optionally fill in:
  9. Seniority Group: Only if this category has different seniority brackets than the agreement default.
  10. Improvement Group: Only if this category has different IT/AT complements than the agreement default.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Labor Agreements in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Solutions for common issues when working with labor agreements.

docs.title: Amounts do not update after applying the agreement
docs.text:
Symptom: You run the Apply action, but some perception scheme lines keep their old amounts.

Cause: The Agreement Change flag is disabled on those lines. This means they are protected as voluntary improvements and the system correctly skipped them.

Solution: - If the protection is intentional, this is expected behavior. - If the protection is accidental, enable the Agreement Change flag on the affected lines and run Apply again.

docs.title: Error when assigning a vacation pay
docs.text:
Symptom: When filling in the Vacation Pay No. field in the agreement header, the system shows an error.

Cause: The selected pay is not of type Vacation. The field only accepts pays of type Vacation.

Solution: Select a pay that is of type Vacation, or create a new pay with that type.

Error message: "Pay No. %1 is not on vacation"

docs.title: Error when entering a coefficient
docs.text:
Symptom: When filling in the Coefficient field on an agreement line, the system shows an error.

Cause A: The line does not have a category assigned. Coefficients are only allowed on lines with a category.

Cause B: The line has a non-zero amount. Coefficient and amount are mutually exclusive.

Solution: - For Cause A: Assign a category to the line before entering the coefficient. - For Cause B: Set the amount to zero before entering the coefficient.

Error messages: - "You should not enter coefficients in the salary levels" - "To enter coefficient, leave the amount at 0"

docs.title: Salary table lines disappear
docs.text:
Symptom: The agreement card lines subpage appears empty even though the agreement has salary data.

Cause: The application date in the header does not match any date that has lines defined.

Solution: Choose the Last Agreement Date action to reposition to the most recent salary table, or use Agreement Dates to select the correct date.

docs.title: Formula does not generate an amount
docs.text:
Symptom: A calculation formula is defined on a line, but the resulting amount is zero.

Cause: - The salary concepts referenced in the formula tokens do not exist in the employee scheme or have zero amounts. - Annual working hours are zero in Payroll Config (if the formula uses token #1). - Circular dependency between formulas.

Solution: 1. Ensure the base concepts referenced in the formula have amounts in the perception scheme. 2. Fill in the annual working hours in Payroll Config. 3. If there is a circular dependency, restructure the formula to eliminate the cycle.

docs.title: Part-time amounts are incorrect
docs.text:
Symptom: After applying the agreement, amounts in the perception scheme are proportionally lower or higher than expected.

Cause: The Weekly Hours value in the agreement header or in the employee contract is incorrect or zero.

Solution: Correct the weekly hours in the agreement header and/or in the employee contract. Run Apply again.

docs.title: Professional category does not appear in lookups
docs.text:
Symptom: When searching for a category in a lookup field, the category does not appear.

Cause: The category has the Blocked field set to Yes, which excludes it from lookups.

Solution: If the category should be available, clear the Blocked field. If it should remain hidden, this is expected behavior.

docs.title: Salary level lines not applied to employee
docs.text:
Symptom: Lines defined by salary level (without category) are not reflected in the employee scheme, even though the employee's category has that salary level.

Cause: A line exists for the same category and same salary concept, which takes priority over the salary level line. The system applies category-level lines first.

Solution: If you want the salary level line to apply, remove the category-level line for that concept. If both should coexist, adjust the amounts on the category-level line.

  • FAQ Labor Agreements

docs.title: Payroll Calculation in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The Payroll Calculation module is the core engine of Omne RH. It transforms employee salary data (perception schemes, contract details, active incidents) into complete payrolls with earnings, deductions, social security contribution bases, and income tax withholdings.

docs.title: How the calculation engine works
docs.text:
The engine processes each payroll in three sequential phases:

  1. Preparation - Validates that the employee has an active contract, locates the applicable perception scheme, and prepares the work calendar for the period.
  2. Main calculation - Calculates earnings (base salary, supplements, overtime), processes sick leave and work accident incidents with benefits, calculates extra pay proration, determines social security contribution bases, and deducts employee contributions.
  3. Finalization - Calculates income tax withholdings, applies advances and automatic deductions (loans, garnishments), records the final payroll, and creates the employee ledger entry.

docs.title: Payroll types
docs.text: Type When to use Monthly payroll Regular monthly calculation Extra pay Summer, Christmas, or other non-prorated extra payments Termination settlement When an employee permanently leaves the company Complementary Adjustments: back pay from labor agreements, salary differences, processing wages Advances Advance payments against future payroll Simulation (Samples) Test calculation without recording definitive data

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• Perception scheme - Defines which salary concepts apply to each employee in a period. Each line contains a salary concept with its calculation key and parameters.
  • Incidents - Sick leave, work accidents, maternity, unpaid leave, and other events that modify the calculation by reducing worked days and generating social security benefits.
  • Payroll header - Contains contribution bases, days contributed, income tax percentage, and general identification data.
  • Payroll lines - Contains each detailed salary concept (earnings, deductions, informational bases).

docs.title: Calculate Payrolls in Batch in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Calculate payrolls for all employees in a contribution unit or the entire company at once. This is the standard operation for monthly payroll closing.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• All employees have active contracts, perception schemes, and complete data.
  • Period incidents are registered for all affected employees.
  • Variable concepts are entered in the perception journal.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  2. Apply the required filters:
  3. Period Start: first day of the month
  4. Period End: last day of the month
  5. Scheme Type: Payroll
  6. Optionally filter by Contribution Unit to process only one location
  7. Select all lines in the list.
  8. Choose Actions > Calculate Payrolls Batch.
  9. The engine processes each employee sequentially. Errors are logged without stopping execution.
  10. When complete, review the error log for employees that were not calculated successfully.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Payroll headers and lines are generated for all processed employees. Employees with errors are recorded in the payroll error log. The system displays a message indicating how many payrolls were calculated successfully and how many had errors.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution Several employees without contracts Verify and renew expired contracts Payroll already calculated Void the existing payroll before recalculating

docs.title: Calculate Complementary Payroll for Back Pay in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a new labor agreement is approved with retroactive effects, calculate salary differences between amounts already paid and the new amounts according to the updated salary tables.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The labor agreement has updated salary tables loaded with the retroactive application date.
  • A perception scheme of type Complementary exists for the affected employees.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Update the labor agreement salary tables with the new application date (for example, January 1 of the retroactive year).
  2. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  3. Filter by Scheme Type = Complementary and the retroactivity period.
  4. Enable the Back Pay flag on the scheme line.
  5. Set the Accrual Year to the year the differences correspond to.
  6. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  7. The engine calculates the differences between the current scheme and the previous scheme for the indicated months.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A payroll header is created with operation type "Complementary". Lines show the salary differences as earnings. Social security contributions are calculated on the differential amounts. Income tax withholding is applied with the "back pay" tax key for special fiscal treatment.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution Difference = 0 Verify the salary table was updated with the correct application date Concept marked as "not retroactive" is omitted This is correct for concepts that should not be retroactive (such as overtime)

• Calculate an individual monthly payroll
  • View payroll history

docs.title: Calculate Extra Pay in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text:
Calculate extra payments (summer bonus, Christmas bonus, or other non-prorated payments) when they are paid separately from the monthly payroll.

If extra payments are prorated monthly, they are automatically included in the regular monthly payroll and this procedure is not needed.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The perception scheme has a record of type Extra Pay configured for the corresponding semester.
  • The extra pay scheme lines have the correct calculation keys and amounts.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by Scheme Type = Extra Pay and the corresponding period.
  3. Select the employee line (or all lines for batch calculation).
  4. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  5. The engine automatically calculates proportionality if the employee was not active for the entire semester.
  6. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll History", and choose the related link.
  7. Filter by operation type Extra Pay to review the result.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A payroll header is created with operation type "Extra Pay". Lines show the extra pay earnings, employee SS contribution, and income tax withholding calculated on the extra pay amounts. If the employee was on leave for part of the semester, the payment is reduced proportionally.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution Extra pay = 0 Verify the extra pay scheme has concepts with amounts assigned Non-proportional payment Review the contract dates to ensure the engine detects partial enrollment

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Calculate an individual monthly payroll
  • View payroll history

docs.title: Calculate an Individual Monthly Payroll in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Calculate the regular monthly payroll for one employee to verify results before running a batch calculation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee has an active contract, an assigned perception scheme, and period incidents registered.
  • Variable concepts (overtime, commissions) are entered in the perception journal.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the scheme line assigned to the employee for the target period.
  3. Verify the Period Start and Period End fields show the correct month dates.
  4. Verify the Scheme Type field is set to Payroll.
  5. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  6. The engine runs the three calculation phases automatically.
  7. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll History", and choose the related link.
  8. Filter by the employee and period to review results.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A payroll header is created with contribution bases, days contributed, and totals. Payroll lines show all earnings (base salary, supplements), deductions (employee SS contribution, income tax withholding), and informational bases. The net amount (earnings minus deductions) is the amount payable to the employee.

docs.title: Calculate Payroll for Part-Time Employees in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Part-time employees have different contribution base calculations: the minimum base is applied per contracted hour instead of the monthly minimum, and professional contingency limits are calculated proportionally to actual hours.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee contract has the Part-Time flag enabled.
  • The employee calendar reflects the scheduled work days for the period.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Verify the contract has the Part-Time flag enabled.
  2. Verify the employee calendar reflects correct work days for the period.
  3. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  4. Filter by the part-time employee.
  5. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  6. The engine detects the part-time contract and:
  7. Calculates permanence days only for scheduled work days
  8. Applies the per-hour minimum base instead of the group monthly minimum
  9. Applies professional contingency limits proportionally to actual hours

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Earnings are calculated according to the calendar permanence days.
  • The contribution base uses: minimum base per hour multiplied by actual hours in the month.
  • The minimum professional contingency limit is: minimum limit per hour multiplied by actual hours.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution Minimum base seems incorrect Verify the contribution group has the per-hour minimum field populated Days contributed = 0 Configure the employee work calendar

docs.title: Calculate Payroll with Sick Leave or Work Accident in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee has an active sick leave (IT) or work accident (AT) incident during the period, the engine automatically adjusts earnings and generates social security benefit lines, company supplement, and company improvement according to configured brackets.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The incident is registered with correct dates and the previous month contribution bases are calculated.
  • Benefit percentages (social security and company) are configured by brackets in the incident card.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by the affected employee and verify the incident has:
  3. Correct start and end dates
  4. Common Contingencies and AT and EP Contribution Base fields populated
  5. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  6. Filter by the employee and the calculation period.
  7. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  8. The engine processes the three phases:
  9. Phase 1: Detects the incident and marks affected days as sick leave in the work calendar.
  10. Phase 2: Calculates proportional earnings for worked days only; generates social security benefit lines and company supplement for sick leave days distributed by brackets.
  11. Phase 3: Calculates income tax on total earnings plus benefits.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Earnings are reduced proportionally to the worked days.
  • Social security benefit lines appear by bracket with configured percentages.
  • Company supplement and company improvement lines appear (if configured in the contribution unit).
  • Contribution bases are adjusted using the previous month IT base for incident days.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution IT benefit = 0 Open the incident and validate the start date to recalculate bases Incorrect days in IT Verify start and end dates in the incident card Company improvement missing Configure the improvement percentage in the contribution unit

docs.title: Calculate Processing Wages in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Processing wages cover the period from the dismissal date to the court ruling date after an unfair dismissal decision. The engine automatically extends the contract period to the processing wages end date.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee contract has the Processing Wages End Date field filled with the court ruling date.
  • A perception scheme of type Complementary with subtype Processing Wages exists.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the employee contract card and set the Processing Wages End Date field to the court ruling date.
  2. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  3. Configure a complementary scheme line with Complementary Type = Processing Wages.
  4. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  5. The engine automatically extends the contract end date to the processing wages date.
  6. Full salaries are calculated from the dismissal date to the ruling date.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A complementary payroll is created with type "Processing Wages" for the corresponding months. The engine ignores the employee termination date and extends calculations to the processing wages end date.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution Nothing is calculated Verify the Processing Wages End Date field is populated in the contract

docs.title: Calculate a Termination Settlement in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee permanently leaves the company, calculate the termination settlement that includes: the proportional part of the current month salary, accrued extra payments, and unused vacation days.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee contract has an end date (company leave) registered.
  • A perception scheme of type Termination Settlement exists for the employee.
  • Pending vacation days are reflected in the employee configuration.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the employee contract card and set the End Date field to the termination date.
  2. Set the Company Leave field to the same termination date.
  3. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  4. Filter by Scheme Type = Termination Settlement and the affected employee.
  5. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  6. The engine automatically calculates:
  7. Proportional earnings for the worked days in the termination month
  8. Prorated extra payments accrued until the termination date
  9. Pending vacation days as additional earnings
  10. Social security contributions and income tax withholdings

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A payroll header is created with operation type "Termination Settlement". The Days Contributed field shows only the worked days in the final month. Lines include proportional earnings, social security contributions, and income tax withholding.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution Contract not active or terminated Verify the termination date matches the calculation period Settlement without proration Extra payments were already prorated monthly (this is expected)

docs.title: Payroll Calculation FAQ in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Answers to common questions about how the payroll calculation engine works.

docs.title: What is the difference between a monthly payroll and an extra pay?
docs.text:
A monthly payroll (type "Payroll") calculates the current month earnings: base salary, supplements, overtime, employee SS deductions, and income tax withholding.

An extra pay (type "Extra Pay") calculates the summer or Christmas bonus when these are not prorated monthly. If extra payments are prorated in 12 monthly installments, they are automatically included as a proration line in each monthly payroll and do not need a separate calculation.

docs.title: What happens if an employee has two active contracts in the same period?
docs.text:
The engine processes each contract independently within the same calculation. If an employee has two active contracts (for example, one ending on day 15 and another starting on day 16), the engine:

  1. Calculates the payroll for the first contract proportionally to its days (1-15).
  2. Calculates the payroll for the second contract proportionally to its days (16-30).

Each segment can have a different perception scheme if the agreement or category changed.

docs.title: Why is net pay different from gross minus tax minus social security?
docs.text:
In addition to the employee SS contribution and income tax withholding, the engine may automatically deduct:

  • Advances pending from previous payrolls
  • Automatic deductions: loans, court garnishments, payments on account
  • Pension plan contributions: employee contributions
  • Benefits in kind: withholding on account that reduces net pay

All these concepts appear as "Deduction" type lines in the payroll detail.

docs.title: What is the difference between back pay and salary differences?
docs.text:
• Back pay (atrasos): Calculated when a new labor agreement is approved with retroactive effects. The engine computes differences between amounts already paid and new amounts. They are declared with the "Back Pay" fiscal marker and the accrual year.
  • Differences: Calculated for one-off errors requiring adjustment (for example, a retroactive category change). Unlike back pay, differences may affect individual concepts only.

The fiscal distinction matters: back pay has special income tax treatment (attributed to the accrual year), while differences are attributed to the current year.

docs.title: What is the difference between a standard complementary payroll and batch complementary payrolls?
docs.text:
A standard complementary payroll (back pay) is calculated from a perception scheme that you configure manually. It produces one complete payroll, with earnings, deductions, contributions, and income tax, for a single period.

Batch complementary payrolls (Generate complementary payrolls in batch) are a different, automated process:

  • They start from an extra pay period to define the contribution periods.
  • They automatically generate the perception scheme lines, prorated month by month.
  • They calculate a complementary payroll for each month, keeping only social security contribution bases (no earnings or income tax lines).
  • They move the employee's contribution to the settlement month's monthly payroll as a single deduction line.

Use batch complementary payrolls when you need to regularize contribution bases for several months retroactively, such as after a change to which salary concepts are subject to contribution for extra pay.

docs.title: How does net-to-gross calculation work?
docs.text:
When a concept has the CALCNETO calculation key, the engine performs an inverse calculation:

  1. Calculates the payroll normally to determine SS and income tax deductions.
  2. Adjusts the gross amount so that after deductions, the net result matches the specified amount exactly.
  3. This adjustment only works with a single CALCNETO concept and no sick leave incidents in the period.

If conditions are not met, the engine disables the adjustment and calculates normally.

docs.title: What happens if I forget to register an incident before calculating?
docs.text:
The engine assumes the employee worked the entire period. This causes overstated earnings and incorrect contribution bases. The solution is:

  1. Void the calculated payroll.
  2. Register the incident with correct dates.
  3. Recalculate the payroll.

It is not possible to add an incident to an already calculated payroll without voiding it first.

docs.title: Can I calculate multiple months at once?
docs.text: No. The engine calculates one period at a time. Each month may depend on the previous month's results (such as IT contribution bases). Calculate each month sequentially.

docs.title: What is the difference between Samples mode and a real calculation?
docs.text: Samples (simulation) mode calculates all amounts identically to a real calculation but does not create employee ledger entries. It can be overwritten without voiding. Use it to verify results before committing to a definitive calculation.

  • Void a calculated payroll

docs.title: Generate Complementary Payrolls in Batch in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Use this procedure to regularize social security contribution bases across several months at once, when an extra pay period requires retroactive adjustments — for example, after a change to which salary concepts are subject to contribution for extra pay. Unlike calculating a single complementary payroll for back pay, this process creates the perception scheme lines, calculates each month's complementary payroll, and moves the employee's social security contribution to the settlement month automatically, in a single run.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The extra pay period (Extra bonus bussiness) has the Calculate initial date and End calculate date fields set.
  • The complementary scheme code is empty, or you accept deleting its existing lines when prompted.
  • The complementary scheme code is not assigned to any contribution unit.
  • If Source payroll type is Monthly, the Prorated price conc. Code field is set (a deduction-type salary concept that receives the employee's contribution in the monthly payroll). This field is not required when the source type is Complementary.
  • Monthly payrolls (or prior complementary payrolls, depending on the source type) are already calculated for the period covered by the extra pay.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Massive complementary generation", and choose the related link.
  2. Fill in the options:
  3. Liquidation date: the target settlement period date.
  4. Source payroll type: Monthly to prorate from the ordinary monthly payroll, or Complementary to prorate from a prior complementary payroll.
  5. Complementary Scheme Code: the scheme code to create or reuse.
  6. Prorated price conc. Code: required when Source payroll type is Monthly.
  7. Enable the phases to run: Create schemes, Calculate complementary, Generate TC's RED.
  8. On the Extra bonus bussiness filter tab, filter by Payment number.
  9. Optionally, filter by Employee No. on the payroll lines filter tab to limit the process to specific employees.
  10. Choose OK.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The process runs in phases automatically: it creates perception scheme lines prorated by employee and month, calculates each month's complementary payroll (keeping only social security contribution bases, with no earnings or income tax lines), and adds a deduction line to the settlement month's monthly payroll for the total employee contribution moved from the complementary payrolls. If enabled, RED TC2 files are also generated for each month in the period.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution "You must enter Complementary Scheme Code and settlement date." Fill in the Complementary Scheme Code and Liquidation date fields "You must enter a value in field Prorated price conc. Code to calculate complementary payroll." Set the Prorated price conc. Code field when Source payroll type is Monthly "Error. You cannot use a Scheme Code assigned in a Quote Unit!" Use a Complementary Scheme Code that is not already assigned to a contribution unit

docs.title: Review the Calculation Error Log in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When the calculation engine encounters errors during processing, it logs them without stopping execution. Always review the error log after batch calculations to identify employees that need corrections.

1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll Registration Errors", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by the calculation period if needed.
  3. Review the error records. Each entry shows:
  4. Employee: the affected employee code
  5. Log Text: error description

docs.title: Run a Payroll Simulation in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before running a definitive payroll calculation, use Samples mode to verify that results are correct. This mode calculates all amounts identically to a real calculation but does not record definitive data or create employee ledger entries.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The same prerequisites as a real calculation (active contract, perception scheme, incidents registered).
  • Previous simulations do not need to be voided; each execution overwrites the prior one.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by the employee or contribution unit to simulate.
  3. Change the Scheme Type field to Samples.
  4. Choose Actions > Calculate Payroll.
  5. The engine calculates all amounts and records them with operation type "Samples".
  6. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll History", and choose the related link.
  7. Filter by operation type Samples to review the results.
  8. Compare earnings, deductions, and net pay with expected values.
  9. Once verified, change the scheme type back to Payroll for the definitive calculation.

docs.text: Payroll lines are calculated with all real amounts. No employee ledger entry is generated. The full breakdown can be reviewed to verify each concept before committing to a definitive calculation.

docs.title: Set Up Payroll Calculation Prerequisites in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before running payroll calculations, verify that all required data is correctly configured. Missing or incorrect data causes calculation errors.

docs.title: Prerequisites checklist
docs.text:
Ensure the following items are configured for each employee to be calculated:

  • Employee has the Calculate payroll field enabled in their card.
  • An active contract covers the calculation period dates.
  • A perception scheme is assigned with a valid application date.
  • The labor agreement is current with updated salary tables.
  • The contribution group is correctly assigned in the contract.
  • Annual contribution limits are up to date.
  • Contribution rates for the social security regime are current.
  • The AT and EP (work accident and occupational disease) heading is assigned.
  • Income tax withholding percentage is calculated or assigned.
  • Period incidents (sick leave, work accidents, permits) are registered.
  • The perception journal is filled in for variable concepts (overtime, commissions).
  • Payroll configuration has rounding precision defined.

docs.title: Step 1: Verify payroll configuration
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll Configuration", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that the Rounding precision (DL) field is set to 2.
  3. Verify that the Direct Settlement System field matches your company setup (Yes for CRETA, No for traditional).

docs.title: Step 2: Verify employee contract
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Employees (Payroll)", and choose the related link.
  2. Open the employee card and navigate to Contracts.
  3. Verify the active contract has:
  4. Start Date on or before the period start
  5. End Date after the period end (or blank for permanent contracts)
  6. Company Leave blank or after the period start
  7. Contribution Group assigned (01 to 11)
  8. Labor Agreement assigned

docs.title: Step 3: Verify perception scheme
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Schemes", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify the employee has an active scheme with an application date on or before the period start.
  3. Verify each scheme line has a Calculation Key assigned.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify contribution limits and rates
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Calculation Limits", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify a record exists with the current year's application date.
  3. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Rates", and choose the related link.
  4. Verify percentages are defined for the contract's regime: common contingencies, unemployment, professional training, and overtime.

docs.title: Step 5: Register period incidents
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. For each employee with active incidents (sick leave, work accident, maternity, unpaid leave):
  3. Verify start and end dates are correct.
  4. For sick leave and work accidents, verify the previous month contribution base fields are populated.

docs.title: Step 6: Fill perception journal (if applicable)
docs.text: If the perception scheme contains variable concepts (overtime, commissions, allowances), enter the values in the perception journal before calculation. Concepts with calculation key FIXED PERIOD or FIXED MONTH are calculated automatically.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: After completing all steps, the system is ready for payroll calculation. Run a simulation (Samples mode) first to verify results before the definitive calculation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Payroll Calculation in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Solutions for common problems encountered during payroll calculation.

docs.title: Recipient without active contract
docs.text:
Symptom: The employee is skipped and the error log shows "Recipient without active contract".

Cause: The engine cannot find a contract with dates covering the calculation period.

Solution: 1. Choose the search icon, enter "Employees (Payroll)", and choose the related link. 2. Open the employee card and navigate to Contracts. 3. Verify a contract exists with: - Start Date on or before the period start - End Date on or after the period end (or blank for permanent) - Company Leave blank or on or after the period start 4. Create or renew the contract if needed, then recalculate.

docs.title: No scheme for the period
docs.text:
Symptom: The error log shows "There is no scheme for period".

Cause: The engine cannot find a perception scheme record with an application date on or before the period start.

Solution: 1. Verify the employee has a perception scheme assigned. 2. Check that the Application Date is on or before the first day of the period. 3. Verify the Labor Agreement in the scheme matches the active contract. 4. If the agreement changed recently, create a new scheme key with the correct application date.

docs.title: Days contributed are zero or incorrect
docs.text:
Symptom: The payroll header shows "Days Contributed = 0" or an unexpected number.

Cause: Calendar not configured (part-time), "Skip day 31" setting active, or incidents absorbing all days.

Solution: - For part-time: verify the employee calendar has correct work days defined. - For day 31 issue: choose the search icon, enter "Company Configuration", and check the "Skip day 31 monthly payment" field. - For incidents: verify incident dates are correct; incorrect dates may absorb the entire period.

docs.title: Social security base does not match manual calculation
docs.text:
Symptom: The common contingencies base differs from the expected manual calculation.

Cause: The base includes prorated extra pay, IT bases from the previous month, and is subject to maximum/minimum limits.

Solution: 1. In payroll lines, filter by concepts with "Subject to SS = Yes" and sum the partial amounts (this is the contributable remuneration). 2. Add the proration (visible in the header Proration field). 3. If there is sick leave, add the previous month IT base. 4. Compare with contribution group limits. The engine applies minimums and maximums automatically. 5. For part-time, limits are calculated per contracted hour.

docs.title: Income tax withholding is zero
docs.text:
Symptom: The payroll calculates correctly but income tax retention is 0.

Cause: Withholding percentage is 0%, all concepts are tax-exempt, or perception keys are missing.

Solution: 1. Check the Withholding Percentage in the employee card (Income Tax tab). 2. If 0%, calculate or manually assign the income tax percentage. 3. Verify scheme lines have a Perception Key assigned (usually "A" for employment income). 4. Verify salary concepts are not all marked as "Tax Exempt".

docs.title: Advances are not deducted
docs.text:
Symptom: The employee has pending advances but the payroll does not include a deduction line.

Solution: 1. Verify advances were registered with Operation Type = Advances (value 4). 2. Check that the advance lines have the "Pay Number" field empty (indicating not yet deducted). 3. Verify the advance period is within the current calculation period range.

docs.title: Sick leave benefits are incorrect
docs.text:
Symptom: Social security benefit and company supplement amounts do not match expected values.

Cause: The previous month daily base is incorrect.

Solution: 1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link. 2. Verify the Common Contingencies field contains the correct previous month base. 3. Verify Days Contributed is correct (usually 30). 4. If bases are wrong, modify the incident start date and re-validate to recalculate bases. 5. Verify benefit brackets (social security % and company %) are correctly configured. 6. Void and recalculate the payroll.

docs.title: Cannot void a posted payroll
docs.text:
Symptom: The system prevents voiding because the payroll is posted.

Solution: 1. First reverse the corresponding accounting entry from the accounting module. 2. Once reversed, the payroll returns to "not posted" state. 3. Proceed to void the payroll normally. 4. Correct data, recalculate, and re-post.

docs.title: Batch calculation is very slow or hangs
docs.text:
Symptom: Batch processing takes excessively long or appears stuck.

Cause: Large employee volume, record locking from concurrent processes, or orphaned records in the intermediate memory table.

Solution: 1. Verify no other user is running a simultaneous calculation on the same employees. 2. Split the calculation into smaller batches (by contribution unit or employee range). 3. If the problem persists, contact the system administrator to check database locks.

docs.title: Back pay complementary calculates zero difference
docs.text:
Symptom: A back pay complementary payroll shows 0 for all amounts.

Solution: 1. Verify the labor agreement salary tables were updated with the new amounts. 2. Check that the Application Date of the new table is on or before the back pay period start. 3. Review salary concepts: those marked "Not Retroactive = Yes" are correctly excluded from the difference calculation.

docs.title: Extra pay proration is missing
docs.text:
Symptom: The payroll header shows "Proration = 0" and the contribution base does not include extra pay proportion.

Solution: 1. Verify the perception scheme has lines for extra pay concepts. 2. Check that extra pay lines have amounts assigned. 3. If extra payments are paid separately (type "Extra Pay"), proration in the monthly payroll is 0 (this is correct behavior).

docs.text:

  • Set up payroll calculation prerequisites
  • Payroll Calculation FAQ

docs.title: View Payroll History in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: After calculating payrolls, review the results to verify that earnings, deductions, contribution bases, and net pay are correct.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • At least one payroll has been calculated in the system.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll History", and choose the related link.
  2. Apply filters:
  3. Employee: employee code
  4. Period: first day of the month
  5. Operation Type: Payroll (or leave blank to see all types)

  7. Common Contingencies: common contingency contribution base
  8. AT and EP: professional contingency contribution base
  9. Days Contributed: days in the period

  16. Quantity: days, hours, or percentage
  17. Amount: unit base

docs.text: The complete payroll detail is displayed. The sum of earnings minus deductions matches the Net Pay field in the header.
