docs.title: Void a Calculated Payroll in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an error is detected in a calculated payroll (incorrect data, unregistered incident, wrong amount), void the payroll before recalculating. Voiding removes the header, lines, and associated employee ledger entry.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The payroll must not be posted (accounting entry created). If already posted, reverse the accounting entry first.
  • The payroll must not be paid. If a bank transfer was generated, void the payment first.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Void Payrolls", and choose the related link. Use "Void Payrolls Batch" to void multiple payrolls at once.
  2. Filter by the employee and the period to void.
  3. Select the payroll to void.
  4. Choose Execute (or Actions > Void).
  5. Confirm the voiding when prompted.
  6. The system removes the payroll header, lines, and reverses the employee ledger entry.
  7. Correct the underlying data (register missing incident, fix contract dates, etc.).
  8. Recalculate the payroll.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The voided payroll disappears from the history. The employee ledger entry is reversed. The employee is available for a new calculation of the same period.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Solution The payroll is posted Reverse the accounting entry before voiding Cannot recalculate after voiding Verify the perception scheme is still valid for the period

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Void payrolls in batch
  • Calculate an individual monthly payroll
  • Review the calculation error log

docs.title: Void Payrolls in Batch in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a widespread error affects multiple payrolls in the same period (for example, incorrect contribution limits), void all affected payrolls at once instead of voiding them individually.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The payrolls must not be posted or paid.
  • Identify the period and employees affected.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Void Payrolls Batch", and choose the related link.
  2. In the request page, set the filters:
  3. Period: the affected month
  4. Operation Type: Payroll
  5. Optionally filter by contribution unit or employee range
  6. Choose OK.
  7. Confirm the batch voiding when prompted.
  8. The system voids all payrolls matching the filters and reverses associated employee ledger entries.
  9. Correct the underlying data (update contribution limits, fix configuration, etc.).
  10. Recalculate the payrolls in batch.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: All payrolls for the selected period are voided. Employee ledger entries are reversed. Employees are available for recalculation.

docs.title: Payroll Payment Overview in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The Payroll Payment module handles the entire payment process after payrolls have been calculated. It covers preparing payments, generating bank files, managing deductions, and communicating banking data to Social Security.

docs.title: Key capabilities
docs.text:
• Prepare payments from calculated payrolls and post them to a payroll journal
  • Generate bank files in SEPA (XML), N34, or N34-1 format for bank submission
  • Configure loans and advances with periodic deductions and interest calculation
  • Manage salary garnishments with automatic calculation per Spanish LEC brackets
  • Communicate bank data to Social Security via CRETA/SLD files
  • Cancel erroneous payments and re-process them

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Calculate payrolls for the period (Payroll Calculation module)
  2. Prepare payments from the calculated payrolls
  3. Review payment lines in the payroll journal
  4. Post payments and generate the bank file
  5. Submit the bank file to your financial institution

docs.title: Related modules
docs.text:
• Payroll Calculation: Must be completed before payments can be prepared
  • Payroll Accounting: Receives posted payment entries for accounting
  • Social Security Affiliation: Shares banking data and contribution units
  • Company Setup: Provides default parameters for interest rates and salary concepts

docs.title: Cancel Erroneous Payments in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: If you detect an error in posted payments, you can cancel them. The system reverses the payment entries, returns the payroll movements to a pending status, and allows you to reprocess them.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Payment entries must exist in the ledger.
  • If payments are already posted to accounting, you must also reverse the accounting entry separately.

docs.title: Cancel the payments
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Cancel Payments", and choose the related link.
  2. On the filter page, filter by the payment documents you want to cancel.
  3. Choose OK.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
The system performs the following actions:

  • Unapplies the payment entries (reverses the application against payroll entries).
  • Deletes the payment entries.
  • The payroll entries return to Pending status and can be paid again.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• If the payments are already posted to accounting, you must reverse the accounting entry separately before or after canceling the payments.
  • Verify that your filters are correct. If no entries are found, check that the document numbers exist and that the filter criteria match.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
After canceling payments:

  1. Correct the erroneous data (employee bank, amounts, or other details).
  2. Run Prepare Payroll Payment again to regenerate the payment lines.
  3. Review and post the corrected payments.

docs.title: Configure an Employee Loan in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a company grants a loan to an employee, you can configure a deduction that automatically discounts a fixed amount from their payroll each month, with optional interest calculation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee must be registered in the system.
  • A discount salary concept must be configured for loans.
  • (Optional) Interest rates must be set up if the loan accrues interest.

docs.title: Create the deduction
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Deductions", and choose Deductions (Payroll).
  2. Choose New to create a record.
  3. Fill in the fields:
  4. Code: An identifier for this deduction (for example, LOAN001).
  5. Description: A description (for example, Employee loan).
  6. Employee No.: Select the employee.
  7. Discount Concept: Select the salary concept for the discount.
  8. No Limit: Clear this checkbox (the loan has a fixed amount).
  9. Payment Method: Select Bank Transfer if repaid via transfer.
  10. If the loan accrues interest:
  11. Enable Accrue Money Value.
  12. Enable Calculate Interest.
  13. Choose Save.

docs.title: Configure periodic deduction
docs.text:
1. From the deductions list, select the deduction you just created.
  2. Choose the Periodic Ded. action in the action bar.
  3. On the Periodic Deductions page, fill in:
  4. Deduction Type: Select All Months (discounted every month).
  5. Period Amount: Enter the monthly repayment amount (for example, 200).
  6. Number of Payments: Enter the total repayment months (for example, 12).
  7. Discount %: Calculated automatically when you enter the number of payments.
  8. Choose Save.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• The deduction is linked to the employee.
  • Each monthly payroll automatically deducts the configured amount.
  • The system calculates interest based on the current rate if interest is enabled.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• The Discount % field automatically recalculates when you modify the Number of Payments in any line. This is expected behavior.
  • Lines with Fixed Percentage enabled keep their percentage unchanged during recalculation.
  • If you see the error "Inconsistency in the type of discounts", you cannot mix certain deduction types in the same code. Review existing lines for conflicts.

docs.title: Configure a Salary Garnishment in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a court orders a salary garnishment on an employee, configure the deduction so that Omne RH automatically calculates the garnishment amount based on the official brackets from the Spanish Civil Procedure Act (LEC, article 607).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee must be registered in the system.
  • A discount salary concept for garnishments must be configured.

docs.title: Create the garnishment deduction
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Deductions", and choose Deductions (Payroll).
  2. Choose New.
  3. Fill in the fields:
  4. Code: An identifier (for example, GARN001).
  5. Description: A description (for example, Judicial garnishment).
  6. Employee No.: Select the affected employee.
  7. Discount Concept: Select the garnishment salary concept.
  8. Mortgage Garnishment: Enable only if the garnishment derives from a mortgage default. This changes the minimum non-attachable amount calculation by considering family members without income.
  9. Simultaneous Withholding: Select Yes only if multiple garnishments must be applied at the same time. Leave blank if they must be applied in queue order by reception date.

docs.title: Configure periodic deduction with garnishment
docs.text:
1. From the deductions list, select the garnishment deduction.
  2. Choose the Periodic Ded. action.
  3. Fill in the fields:
  4. Salary Garnishment: Enable this checkbox. If the Deduction Type field is empty, it is automatically set to All Months and Extra Pays. If a type was already selected, it remains unchanged.
  5. LEC Brackets Code: Leave blank to use the official brackets from LEC article 607. If the court specifies custom percentages, select a configured brackets code.
  6. Additional Net Salary to Withhold: If there is additional income that must be considered in the calculation, enter the amount.
  7. Choose Save.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• The garnishment is automatically applied in all monthly payrolls and extra pays for the employee.
  • The calculation respects the minimum wage (SMI) as the non-attachable minimum.
  • If mortgage garnishment is enabled, family members without income are factored into the calculation.

docs.title: Multiple garnishments
docs.text:
When an employee has more than one garnishment:

  • If Simultaneous Withholding is set to Yes on all deductions, they are all applied at the same time.
  • If left blank, garnishments are applied in queue order based on their reception date.
  • Verify the order of priority after posting payrolls.

docs.title: Payroll Payment FAQ in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Common questions and answers about the payroll payment process in Omne RH.

docs.title: What is the difference between Post and Post and Transfer?
docs.text:
When posting the payroll journal, the system presents two options:

  • Post: Only confirms the payments in the system. You must generate the bank file manually afterward.
  • Post and Transfer: Confirms the payments and automatically opens the bank file generation page. This is the fastest option if you plan to submit transfers immediately.

Use Post and Transfer unless you need to review payments before generating the file.

docs.title: Which bank file format should I choose: SEPA, N34, or N34-1?
docs.text:
Format When to use SEPA Recommended for most current banks. European standard XML format. N34 Only if your bank specifically requires it. Classic Spanish text format. N34-1 If you need international transfers in the classic format.

If you are unsure, check with your financial institution. Most Spanish banks have accepted SEPA for years.

docs.title: What happens if an employee has partial payment across multiple banks?
docs.text:
The system handles this automatically. When an employee has partial payment configured:

  • The payment preparation generates multiple lines for the same employee, one per bank.
  • The amount is distributed according to the employee bank percentage configuration.
  • Each line carries its own destination bank.

No manual intervention is required.

docs.title: Can I modify journal lines before posting?
docs.text:
Yes. After running Prepare Payroll Payment and before choosing Post, you can:

  • Correct amounts.
  • Change the destination bank.
  • Delete lines that should not be paid this month.
  • Add lines manually.

Changes are preserved until you post the journal.

docs.title: How do I know which payrolls are pending payment?
docs.text:
Payrolls pending payment are those with a Pending status. You can check this in two ways:

  1. From the Role Center: KPI indicators show the number of pending payrolls and active employees for the period.
  2. From Prepare Payment: The preparation process only includes pending entries with a non-zero amount.

If no records appear when preparing payments, all payrolls have already been paid, or no payrolls have been calculated for that period.

docs.title: How does the automatic percentage recalculation work in deductions?
docs.text:
When an employee has multiple periodic deduction lines with the same code:

  1. Lines with Fixed Percentage enabled keep their percentage unchanged.
  2. The remaining lines share the remaining percentage equally.
  3. The system calculates: % per line = (100% - total fixed %) / total number of payments.

This recalculation runs automatically when you modify the Number of Payments or Discount % in any line.

docs.title: What is the difference between Bank Transfer File and Create Transfer File?
docs.text:
Aspect Bank Transfer File Create Transfer File Generates printed list Yes No Supports UTF-8 No Yes Output format ZIP (file + list) Direct file Typical use File + audit report Only the bank file needed

Use Create Transfer File if your bank rejects the file due to special characters, as it supports UTF-8 encoding.

docs.title: Can I cancel a posted payment?
docs.text:
Yes. Use Cancel Payments (choose the search icon, enter "Cancel Payments"):

  • The system reverses the payment application against payroll entries.
  • Payment entries are deleted.
  • Affected payrolls return to Pending status.

If the payment was already posted to accounting, you must also reverse the accounting entry.

docs.title: What is CRETA and when do I need it?
docs.text:
CRETA is the electronic communication system with the Spanish Social Security (TGSS). The module generates SLD (Bank Data) files to:

  • Communicate the bank assigned to each contribution unit.
  • Report bank changes.
  • Request deletion of bank assignments.

You need it when you register a new contribution unit, change a bank for a contribution unit, or when the TGSS requests bank data confirmation.

docs.title: Generate a SEPA Bank File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: After posting payroll payments, generate a bank transfer file to submit payment orders to your financial institution. Omne RH supports SEPA (XML), N34, and N34-1 formats.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Payments must be posted in the payroll journal.
  • Banks in the catalog must have a valid SWIFT Code (for SEPA format).
  • Employees must have valid IBAN numbers.

docs.title: Generate the bank file
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Bank Transfer File", and choose the related link.
  2. On the filter page, set:
  3. Document No.: The range of payment documents to include.
  4. Document Type: Filter by Payment and/or Withholding Deposit.
  5. On the Options tab, set:
  6. Standard: Select SEPA (recommended for most current banks). Alternatively, select N34 or N34-1 for legacy formats.
  7. Choose OK.

The system generates a compressed ZIP file containing the bank file in the selected format and a printed list of included transfers.

docs.title: Choose the right format
docs.text: Format When to use SEPA Recommended for most current banks. European standard XML format. N34 Only if your bank specifically requires it. Classic Spanish text format. N34-1 If you need to include international transfers in the classic format.

docs.title: Alternative: Create Transfer File (UTF-8)
docs.text:
If your bank rejects the file due to special characters, use the alternative report:

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Create Transfer File", and choose the related link.
  2. On the Options tab, select Encoding: UTF-8.
  3. Choose OK.

This option generates the file directly without a printed list but supports full UTF-8 encoding.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Issue Solution Bank rejects file (invalid IBAN) Verify all employees have a valid IBAN in their bank setup Bank rejects file (missing SWIFT) Add the SWIFT code to the bank in Banks (Payroll) Special character rejection Use Create Transfer File with UTF-8 encoding instead

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Prepare and post payroll payments
  • Set up payroll payment

docs.title: Prepare and Post Payroll Payments in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: After payrolls are calculated for a period, you prepare payment lines in the payroll journal, review them, and post the payments to generate bank transfer records.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Payrolls for the period must be calculated and in Pending status.
  • The payroll journal book and section must exist.
  • Employees must have valid bank accounts assigned.

docs.title: Prepare the payments
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Prepare Payroll Payment", and choose the related link.
  2. On the filter page, set:
  3. Posting Date: The date range for the period (for example, 01/01/2026..31/01/2026).
  4. Document Type: Select Payroll or leave blank to include all types.
  5. On the Options tab, set:
  6. Payroll Journal Book: Select your working book (for example, PAYROLL).
  7. Payroll Journal Section: Select the section (for example, GENERIC).
  8. Choose OK.

The system creates payment lines in the journal, one for each employee with a pending payroll. If an employee has partial payment across multiple banks, multiple lines are generated.

docs.title: Review the journal
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll Journal", and choose the related link.
  2. Review the generated lines:
  3. Verify that the Employee No. and Amount are correct.
  4. Check the assigned Payment Bank No.
  5. You can manually correct any data before posting.

docs.title: Post the payments
docs.text:
1. In the payroll journal, choose the Post action (or go to Actions > Posting > Post).
  2. Select one of the options:
  3. Post: Only posts the payments.
  4. Post and Transfer: Posts the payments and automatically opens the bank file generation page.
  5. Confirm the operation.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Payment entries are recorded in the ledger.
  • If you chose Post and Transfer, the bank file generation page opens automatically.
  • The journal is cleared and ready for the next period.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Error message Cause Solution "There is nothing to register" No lines in the journal Run Prepare Payroll Payment first "Cannot contain a filter when posting a periodic journal" Date filters active on a periodic journal Remove all filters from the journal before posting

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Generate a SEPA bank file
  • Cancel erroneous payments

docs.title: Set Up Payroll Payment in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before you can process payroll payments, you must configure the bank catalog, verify employee bank data, and optionally set up interest rates for loans.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Employees must be registered with complete bank data (IBAN)
  • Payrolls for the period must be calculated and posted
  • The bank catalog must include SWIFT codes for SEPA file generation

docs.title: Set up the bank catalog
docs.text:
Banks are required to generate SEPA transfer files.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Banks", and choose Banks (Payroll).
  2. For each bank, fill in the following fields:
  3. Code: A 4-character bank identifier (for example, 0049).
  4. Bank Name: The full name of the financial institution.
  5. SWIFT Code: The BIC code of the bank (required for SEPA files).

[!IMPORTANT] The SWIFT Code field is mandatory for SEPA file generation. Without it, the bank will reject the file.

docs.title: Verify employee bank accounts
docs.text:
Each employee must have a bank assigned with a complete IBAN.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Employees (Payroll)", and choose the related link.
  2. Select the employee, then choose Employee Bank.
  3. Verify that:
  4. The IBAN field is complete (ES format + 22 digits).
  5. The CCC (Account Code) is correct.
  6. The bank is linked to a code from the bank catalog.

docs.title: Set up interest rates (loans only)
docs.text:
If your company grants employee loans, configure the applicable interest rates.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Interest rate", and choose Interest Rate and Money Value.
  2. Fill in the fields:
  3. Start Date: The date from which the rate applies.
  4. Interest %: The annual interest percentage.
  5. Money Value %: The money value percentage.
  6. Interest Concept Code: Automatically filled from Company Setup.
  7. Money Value Concept Code: Automatically filled from Company Setup.

docs.title: Configure default deduction settings (loans only)
docs.text:
If your company manages loans or advances, configure default values in Company Setup.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Company Setup", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that Accrue Money Value and Calculate Interest are enabled if you want new deductions to inherit these values automatically.

docs.title: Verification checklist
docs.text:
After completing the setup, verify:

  • The bank catalog has at least one entry with a SWIFT code.
  • Main employees have a bank assigned with a valid IBAN.
  • Payrolls for the period are calculated.
  • (If using loans) Interest rate is configured with a current start date.
  • (If using CRETA) Contribution units have an assigned bank.

docs.title: Quick test
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Prepare Payment", and choose the related link.
  2. Select a date range for the current period.
  3. The system should display payroll records pending payment.
  4. If no records appear, verify that payrolls are calculated and that entries have a Pending status.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Prepare and post payroll payments
  • Configure an employee loan

docs.title: Submit Bank Data to Social Security in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Use the CRETA/SLD communication to inform the Spanish Social Security (TGSS) about the bank accounts assigned to your contribution units. This is required when you register a new contribution unit, change its bank, or when the TGSS requests bank data confirmation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Contribution units must be configured with an assigned bank account.
  • The bank catalog must contain the bank codes for the contribution units.

docs.title: Generate the CRETA file
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "SLD Bank Data", and choose the related link.
  2. On the filter page, set:
  3. Name: Select the company (if you work with multiple companies).
  4. Contribution Regime: Filter by regime if you only need to communicate specific units.
  5. On the Options tab, set:
  6. Notify: Select the action to perform:
    • Contribution Unit Bank: Communicate the currently assigned bank.
    • New Bank: Communicate a bank change (you must specify the new bank code).
    • Delete Bank: Request deletion of the bank assignment.
  7. Balance Type: Select Both (most common).
  8. Save Bank: Enable to save the assignment in the system.
  9. Choose OK.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system generates an XML file in CRETA format for submission to the Social Security through the RED/SLD system. If you enabled Save Bank, the assignment is recorded in the system.

docs.title: When to use CRETA
docs.text: Scenario Notify option New contribution unit registered Contribution Unit Bank Bank account changed for a unit New Bank TGSS requests bank data confirmation Contribution Unit Bank Removing a bank assignment Delete Bank

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
After generating the file:

  1. Submit the XML file to Social Security through the RED/SLD system.
  2. Verify the acceptance of the communication.
  3. If rejected, review the bank data and regenerate.

docs.text:
• Set up payroll payment

docs.title: Troubleshooting Payroll Payment in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Solutions for common problems encountered when processing payroll payments in Omne RH.

docs.title: "There is nothing to register" when posting the journal
docs.text:
Cause: The payroll journal has no payment lines.

Solution:

  1. Verify you are in the correct journal book and section.
  2. Run Prepare Payroll Payment first (choose the search icon, enter "Prepare Payroll Payment").
  3. If you already ran it and still see no lines, verify that payrolls are calculated for the selected period.

docs.title: "Cannot contain a filter when posting a periodic journal"
docs.text:
Cause: A periodic journal does not allow date filters to be active during posting.

Solution:

  1. Remove all active filters from the journal, especially Posting Date filters.
  2. Choose the filter icon and clear all filters.
  3. Try posting again.

docs.title: Bank rejects the SEPA file
docs.text:
Cause: The most common reasons are invalid IBAN, missing SWIFT code, or unsupported special characters.

Solution by cause:

docs.title: Invalid IBAN or missing SWIFT
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Banks (Payroll)", and verify the bank has a SWIFT Code.
  2. Open the affected employee card, choose Employee Bank, and verify the IBAN is complete.
  3. Regenerate the file.

docs.title: Special characters
docs.text:
1. Instead of Bank Transfer File, use Create Transfer File (choose the search icon, enter "Create Transfer File").
  2. On the Options tab, select Encoding: UTF-8.
  3. Generate the file again.

docs.title: "Inconsistency in the type of discounts" in periodic deductions
docs.text:
Cause: Certain deduction types cannot coexist in the same deduction code.

Incompatible combinations:

If a line exists with You cannot add All Months and Extra Pays Another All Months and Extra Pays, All Months, or All Extra Pays All Months Another All Months or All Months and Extra Pays All Extra Pays Another All Extra Pays or All Months and Extra Pays Month (specific) Another line with the same month Extra Pay (specific) Another line with the same extra pay

Solution:

  1. Review all existing lines for the deduction.
  2. Delete or modify the conflicting line.
  3. If you need specific months, use the Month type with a specific month on each line.

docs.title: Discount percentages change unexpectedly in deductions
docs.text:
Cause: This is expected behavior. The system automatically redistributes percentages so they total 100%.

How it works:

  • Lines with Fixed Percentage enabled are not modified.
  • Remaining lines share the leftover percentage equally.

Solution:

  • To prevent a percentage from changing, enable Fixed Percentage on that line before entering the value.
  • If you only need to specify the number of payments, let the system calculate the percentage automatically.

docs.title: "Prepare Payment" generates no lines
docs.text:
Cause: No payrolls with Pending status exist for the selected period.

Solution:

  1. Broaden your filters: clear the Document Type filter and expand the date range.
  2. Verify that payrolls are calculated for the period by checking the payroll ledger.
  3. Check that payments have not already been posted. Previously paid payrolls are no longer in Pending status.

docs.title: "Renaming the blank code is not allowed" when editing a deduction
docs.text:
Cause: The blank-code record is a special system record that cannot be renamed.

Solution:

  1. Do not attempt to rename this record.
  2. Create a new deduction with the desired code instead.
  3. Configure the required data on the new record.
  4. Reassign references in the affected employees.

docs.title: Perception Schemes Overview in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Perception schemes define the individualized salary structure for each employee in payroll. A scheme groups the salary concepts (earnings, deductions, bases, costs) that determine how payroll is calculated, including fixed amounts, monthly variables, and automatic calculation formulas.

docs.title: Scheme header
docs.text:
A scheme header is a template that defines the payroll type. Each header specifies whether the scheme applies to monthly payroll, extra pay, advances, or supplementary pay.

Payroll type Purpose Monthly Regular monthly payroll Extra Pay Extraordinary payments (June, December, etc.) Advances Payroll advances Supplementary Arrears, regularizations, etc.

docs.title: Scheme key
docs.text: A scheme key links an employee to a specific scheme, labor agreement, and application date. This combination allows multiple versions of a scheme over time, for example when amounts are updated due to an agreement revision.

docs.title: Scheme line
docs.text: Each line represents a salary concept within the scheme. It contains the amount or calculation formula, concept type (earning, deduction, base, text, cost), and properties affecting social security contributions, income tax, proration, and monthly variability.

docs.title: Perception journal
docs.text: A temporary worksheet for bulk entry of variable perceptions. It collects variable concepts from multiple employees, allows editing of period amounts, and posts them in bulk to their respective schemes.

docs.title: Variable perceptions
docs.text: Salary concepts with amounts that change every month (commissions, overtime, variable bonuses). The "Variable" flag on a scheme line enables the concept to be collected in the perception journal for periodic updates.

docs.title: Calculation formulas
docs.text: Expressions that reference other concepts within the same scheme to calculate amounts automatically. The system uses an internal engine that processes inter-concept expressions, so that changing one field recalculates dependent formulas.

docs.title: Who uses this module
docs.text: Role Main use Payroll technician Configure and maintain schemes, register monthly variable perceptions, manage advances HR manager Review salary structure, check annual gross amounts Functional consultant Configure scheme templates by agreement, automate salary variations

docs.title: How it relates to other modules
docs.text:
• Labor agreements provide categories and available concepts to the scheme
  • Employees are individually assigned to schemes
  • Salary concepts define the concepts referenced in scheme lines
  • Payroll calculation uses scheme lines as the calculation basis
  • Income tax (IRPF) handles regularization after net advances
  • Payroll accounting uses the accounting group from each concept line

  • Create a Perception Scheme

docs.title: Calculate Payroll from a Perception Scheme in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The perception scheme card lets you run individual payroll calculation for an employee without going to the batch payroll process. You can also calculate extra pays and termination settlements from this page.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The perception scheme is complete with all necessary salary concepts.
  • Monthly variable perceptions are registered (if applicable).
  • Income tax withholding (IRPF) is configured for the employee.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Scheme Dates", and choose the related link.
  2. Select the employee's scheme and open the card.
  3. Choose the appropriate action based on payroll type:
  4. Post Payroll (F9): For regular monthly payroll.
  5. Post Payroll Batch: For batch payroll from this page.
  6. Post Extra Pay: For extraordinary payments.
  7. Post Termination Settlement: For termination settlements.
  8. Verify the result by choosing Payroll List (Shift+Ctrl+N).

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The payroll is calculated and posted. You can view it in the employee's payroll history.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If you receive "You have pending lines in the Change Journal", go to the perception journal and post or delete the pending lines before calculating payroll.
  • If the scheme does not appear in batch payroll runs, check that the Sporadic option is disabled on the scheme header.
  • To review annual statistics, use the Statistics action (Shift+Ctrl+J).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Create a Perception Scheme
  • Register Variable Perceptions
  • Perception Schemes Overview

docs.title: Copy a Perception Scheme in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a new employee has the same salary conditions as an existing one, or when you need a new scheme version with a different application date due to a salary revision, you can copy a complete scheme with all its lines.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A source scheme with configured lines exists.
  • The target employee is registered (if copying between employees).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Scheme Dates", and choose the related link. Or open the scheme card directly.
  2. Choose the Copy Scheme action.
  3. Fill in the parameters:
  4. From Scheme: The source scheme (for example, MES01).
  5. From Date: The source scheme date (for example, 01/01/2025).
  6. Last Existing: Enable to automatically select the latest application date from the source scheme.
  7. To Scheme: The target scheme (can be the same or a different one).
  8. To Date: The new application date (for example, 01/07/2025).
  9. Choose OK.
  10. If the target scheme already exists, the system asks whether to delete and replace it. Confirm to proceed.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A new scheme key is created with the target date and all lines copied from the source. Amounts are kept identical and must be manually adjusted if there is a salary variation.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• After copying, use the Salary Variation action to apply percentage increases in bulk.
  • If you receive "Target scheme already exists", confirm the deletion or choose a different date.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Create a Perception Scheme
  • Delete a Perception Scheme

docs.title: Create a Perception Scheme in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee joins the company or their salary conditions change, you must create or update their perception scheme to reflect the applicable salary concepts.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee is registered with an active contract and assigned labor agreement.
  • Salary concepts are defined in the agreement or at a general level.
  • A scheme header exists with the correct payroll type.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Scheme Dates", and choose the related link.
  2. Choose New to create a record.
  3. Fill in the fields:
  4. Employee No.: Select the employee.
  5. Perception Scheme: Select the scheme header (for example, MES01).
  6. Labor Agreement: This is filled automatically from the employee's contract. Verify it is correct.
  7. Application Date: Enter the date from which this scheme is effective.
  8. Choose the line to open the scheme card (Perception Schemes).
  9. In the lines subpage, add each salary concept:
  10. Salary Concept: Select the concept (for example, 0001 for base salary). The description, concept type, and contribution properties are filled automatically.
  11. Amount: Enter the monthly amount.
  12. Repeat for each additional concept (agreement bonus, withholding, etc.).
  13. Verify that the Annual Gross Amount and Annual Cost Amount fields in the header display correct totals.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The scheme is configured with all the employee's salary concepts. Annual amounts are automatically calculated in the header. The scheme is ready for payroll calculation.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If the annual gross amount shows zero, close and reopen the scheme card to refresh the calculated field.
  • If the concept type does not load when you select a concept, verify that the salary concept card has a type defined.
  • If the category does not fill in automatically, check that the employee has an active contract.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Set Up Perception Schemes
  • Register Variable Perceptions
  • Copy a Perception Scheme

docs.title: Delete a Perception Scheme in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a scheme is no longer needed (employee terminated, configuration error, or duplicate scheme), you can delete it completely along with all its lines.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The scheme must not be in use by an active payroll calculation.
  • Deletion is permanent: all lines and the scheme key are removed.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Scheme Dates", and choose the related link. Or open the scheme card directly.
  2. Choose the Delete Scheme action.
  3. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: All scheme lines and the scheme key are deleted. The employee no longer has that scheme assigned for the specified date.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If the scheme still appears after deleting, verify that you confirmed the deletion prompt.
  • If you deleted by mistake, you can recreate the scheme or copy it from another existing scheme.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Create a Perception Scheme
  • Copy a Perception Scheme

docs.title: Perception Schemes FAQ in Omne RH Payroll
What is the difference between the Amount and Variable Amount fields?
docs.text:
The Amount field contains the fixed monthly value of a concept (for example, a base salary of 1,800.00 that does not change). When a concept is marked as Variable, the Variable Amount and Variable Quantity fields appear, allowing you to register values that change monthly through the perception journal, without modifying the fixed base amount.

A concept can have both a fixed amount and a variable amount simultaneously. Payroll calculation uses both according to the concept rules.

docs.title: What happens if I copy a scheme and the target already exists?
docs.text:
The system shows a confirmation dialog. If you confirm, the target scheme is completely deleted (all lines and the key) and replaced with the lines from the source scheme. Amounts are copied as-is. If there is a salary revision, you must update amounts manually or use the Salary Variation action.

The Last Existing option in the copy dialog automatically selects the latest application date from the source scheme.

docs.title: How does the Sporadic option affect payroll calculation?
docs.text:
A scheme with Sporadic enabled is not included in batch payroll calculation runs. It is only processed when you run individual calculation from the scheme card using the Post Payroll (F9) action.

This is useful for supplementary or termination schemes that are calculated on demand and should not interfere with regular monthly payroll.

docs.title: What is the difference between a Gross advance and a Net advance?
docs.text:
Type Calculation Tax regularization Gross The amount is advanced as-is, without deductions Not triggered Net Net = Gross minus social security minus income tax Automatic

A net advance requires that all lines in the same posting belong to the same period (month). If there are lines from different months, you must post them separately.

docs.title: What does the Agreement Change flag mean on scheme lines?
docs.text:
When a line has Agreement Change set to Yes, that line is not automatically updated when you run agreement change or salary variation processes. It is marked automatically when a user manually customizes an amount that originally came from the labor agreement.

This is a protection mechanism: if an employee has an individual arrangement for a concept that differs from the agreement table, this flag prevents a bulk agreement update from overwriting that arrangement.

docs.title: How does automatic variable grouping in the journal work?
docs.text:
If the Sum Var. Perception Journal option is enabled in company setup, the system automatically groups journal lines with the same salary concept before posting to the scheme. For example, if there are three lines for "Commissions" with amounts of 100, 200, and 150, a single line with amount 450 is posted.

If disabled, each line is processed individually and may trigger the Replace/Add dialog for duplicates.

docs.title: Can an employee have multiple schemes?
docs.text:
Yes. An employee can have multiple schemes with different combinations of header, agreement, and date. A typical setup includes: - A Monthly scheme for regular payroll - An Extra Pay scheme for extraordinary payments - Optionally, Supplementary schemes for arrears or regularizations

Each scheme has its own key identified by employee + scheme + agreement + application date.

docs.title: How is the Annual Amount on a line calculated?
docs.text:
It depends on the Calculation Key assigned to the line:

Key Formula MONTHLY Amount x 12 DN (Natural days) Amount x 365 DT (Working days) Amount x 247 No key Amount without multiplier

The annual amount recalculates automatically whenever the line amount is modified. The sum of annual amounts for Earning-type concepts is shown in the header as Annual Gross Amount.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Perception Schemes Overview
  • Troubleshooting Perception Schemes

docs.title: Generate a Net Advance in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: You can advance part of an employee's pay before the regular payroll calculation. A net advance automatically deducts social security contributions and income tax withholding from the gross amount, and regularizes the tax withholding percentage.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee's scheme is configured with the concepts that will generate the advance.
  • A deduction code for advances is configured.
  • A payroll journal book and section are configured to receive the advance entry.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Journal Sections", and choose the related link. Then choose Edit Journal.
  2. Locate or create the line for the concept to advance.
  3. Set the Advance field to Yes.
  4. Select the advance type:
  5. Net: Deducts social security and income tax. Triggers automatic tax regularization.
  6. Gross: Advances the full amount without deductions.
  7. Fill in the required fields:
  8. Advance Deduction Code: The deduction code for the advance.
  9. Payroll Journal Book: The target journal book.
  10. Payroll Journal Section: The target journal section.
  11. Posting Date: The date for the accounting entry.
  12. Choose Post Journal (F9).
  13. The system performs two internal steps:
  14. Posts the line and marks it for income tax regularization.
  15. Regularizes the income tax and generates the advance with the calculated net amount.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The advance is posted to the payroll journal with the net calculated amount. The employee's income tax withholding percentage is automatically regularized. The line is removed from the perception journal.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If you receive the error "You must inform the deduction code of the advance", fill in the Advance Deduction Code field before posting.
  • If you receive "You must report the book and section of the payroll journal", fill in both journal book and section fields.
  • If you receive "Error, cannot be anticipated to net. There are 2 different periods", post advances from different months in separate operations.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Register Variable Perceptions
  • Perception Schemes Overview

docs.title: Handle Duplicate Concepts in Journal Posting in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When you post the perception journal, the system may detect that a line with the same salary concept and overlapping period already exists in the scheme. You must choose whether to replace or add the new amount.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The perception journal has lines ready to post.
  • The target scheme already contains lines with the same concept and overlapping periods.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose Post Journal (F9).
  2. If duplicates are detected, a dialog appears with two options:
  3. Replace: Overwrites the existing line with the new values.
  4. Add: Accumulates the new amount on top of the existing one.
  5. The choice applies to all duplicate lines in the same posting.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Replace: The scheme line contains only the new amount.
  • Add: The scheme line contains the sum of both amounts. If both lines have non-zero quantities, the system calculates a weighted average.

docs.title: When to use each option
docs.text:
• Use Add when you receive partial amounts from different sources (for example, sales commissions by region).
  • Use Replace when you are correcting an incorrect amount.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If the posting stops with "Process canceled by the user", it means both options were rejected. You must choose either Replace or Add to continue.
  • To avoid the duplicate dialog, review the journal lines and remove duplicates before posting.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Register Variable Perceptions
  • Create a Perception Scheme

docs.title: Register Variable Perceptions in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Variable concepts like commissions, overtime, or shift bonuses require monthly updates before payroll calculation. The perception journal lets you manage this update in bulk for multiple employees.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Perception schemes are configured with concepts marked as Variable.
  • At least one perception journal section is configured.
  • You have the variable amounts for the period (from spreadsheets, control files, etc.).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Journal Sections", and choose the related link.
  2. Select the working section and choose Edit Journal.
  3. Run the Collect Variable Perceptions action:
  4. Month: Enter the month to process (for example, 2 for February). This field is required.
  5. Clear Previous Month Quantity: Enable to reset quantities from the prior month.
  6. Clear Previous Month Amount: Enable to reset amounts from the prior month.
  7. Choose OK.
  8. The system populates the journal with all variable concept lines from the filtered employees' schemes.
  9. Update amounts and quantities for the current period:
  10. Variable Amount: The variable amount for the month.
  11. Variable Quantity: The quantity factor (hours, days, units).
  12. Period Start / Period End: The dates of the accrual period.
  13. Optionally, for bulk loading, choose Import Excel to load data from an external file.
  14. Choose Post Journal (F9) to transfer the amounts to each employee's scheme.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The variable amounts are recorded in the corresponding scheme lines. Journal lines are deleted after successful posting. If the Sum Var. Perception Journal option is enabled in company setup, lines with the same concept are automatically grouped before posting.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If you receive the error "Must inform month to register", enter a value between 1 and 12 in the Month field.
  • If variables remain at zero after posting, verify that the "Clear Previous Month" options are disabled and that the line period dates overlap with the working month.
  • If a new line appears in the scheme instead of updating the existing one, verify that the salary concept, accounting group, and date range match the existing line.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Handle Duplicate Concepts in Journal Posting
  • Generate a Net Advance
  • Create a Perception Scheme

docs.title: Set Up Perception Schemes in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before you can create and manage perception schemes, you must configure master data, scheme headers, and perception journal sections.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Requirement Where to verify Employees registered Choose the search icon, enter "Employees (Payroll)", and choose the related link Labor agreements configured Choose the search icon, enter "Labor Agreements", and choose the related link Salary concepts defined Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link Calculation keys defined Choose the search icon, enter "Calculation Keys", and choose the related link Contribution units configured Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Units", and choose the related link Extra pays set up Choose the search icon, enter "Company Extra Pays", and choose the related link

The user must have read and write permissions on perception scheme objects in the Omne RH permission set.

docs.title: Step 1: Configure scheme headers
docs.text:
Scheme headers act as templates that define the payroll type.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Scheme Headers", and choose the related link.
  2. Choose New to create a header.
  3. Fill in the fields:
  4. Name: An identifier code (up to 10 characters), for example MES01 or PEXT01.
  5. Description: A descriptive text, for example "Standard monthly payroll".
  6. Payroll Type: Select the applicable type: Monthly, Extra Pay, Advances, or Supplementary.
  7. Sporadic: Select this option only if the scheme should be excluded from batch payroll calculations.
  8. Repeat for each scheme header you need.

A sporadic scheme is only calculated when you run payroll individually from the scheme card. It is not included in batch runs.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure perception journal sections
docs.text:
If you use variable perceptions, you need at least one active journal section.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Journal Sections", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that at least one section exists and is active.
  3. From the section, choose Edit Journal to open the perception journal.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure company settings (optional)
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll Setup", and choose the related link.
  2. Review the Sum Var. Perception Journal option:
  3. If enabled, the system automatically groups journal lines with the same salary concept before posting.
  4. If disabled, each line is processed individually.

This automatic grouping is useful when importing data from external sources where the same concept may appear on multiple lines.

docs.title: Verify the configuration
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Scheme Dates", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that you can create records by specifying employee, scheme, agreement, and date.
  3. Open a scheme card and confirm that the lines subpage allows adding salary concepts.
  4. Verify that the annual amounts (gross and cost) are calculated correctly in the header.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Perception Schemes Overview
  • Create a Perception Scheme

docs.title: Troubleshooting Perception Schemes in Omne RH Payroll
Pending lines in the Change Journal
docs.text:
Error: "You have pending lines in the Change Journal"

This error appears when you try to calculate payroll from the scheme card but there are unposted lines in the perception journal for this employee.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Journal Sections", and choose the related link. Then choose Edit Journal.
  2. Find the pending lines for the affected employee.
  3. Either post the lines (F9) to incorporate the values, or delete them if they are not needed.
  4. Return to the scheme card and retry the payroll calculation.

docs.title: Must inform month to register
docs.text:
Error: "Must inform month to register"

This error appears when running Collect Variable Perceptions without specifying a month.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: Enter a value between 1 and 12 in the Month field when running the Collect Variable Perceptions action. If you see "Wrong month", verify the value is within the valid range.

docs.title: Variable perceptions remain at zero after posting
docs.text: Symptom: You collect variable perceptions and post with F9, but amounts in the schemes stay at zero.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. When running Collect Variable Perceptions, disable the Clear Previous Month Quantity and Clear Previous Month Amount options if you want to keep previous values.
  2. Verify that the Period Start and Period End dates on each journal line are consistent with the working month.
  3. Post again with F9.

docs.title: New line created instead of updating existing
docs.text: Symptom: After posting the journal, a new line appears in the scheme for the same concept instead of updating the existing one.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
The system matches by salary concept + accounting group + period overlap. Verify that:

  1. The salary concept on the journal line matches the one in the scheme.
  2. The accounting group is the same.
  3. The date range (Period Start / Period End) on the journal line overlaps with the existing scheme line.

docs.title: Cannot anticipate to net with different periods
docs.text:
Error: "Error, cannot be anticipated to net. There are 2 different periods"

This occurs when lines marked as Net Advance in the same posting belong to different months.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: Post advances from each month separately. Alternatively, change conflicting lines to Gross advance type if they do not require social security and tax deductions.

docs.title: Missing advance fields
docs.text:
Error: "You must inform the deduction code of the advance" or "You must report the book and section of the payroll journal"

These appear when lines are marked as Advance but required fields are empty.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Before posting, fill in these fields on the advance line:

  1. Advance Deduction Code
  2. Payroll Journal Book
  3. Payroll Journal Section

docs.title: Scheme not included in batch payroll
docs.text: Symptom: The employee is skipped when running batch payroll calculation.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Scheme Headers", and choose the related link.
  2. Find the affected scheme header.
  3. Disable the Sporadic option.
  4. Run the batch calculation again.

docs.title: Annual Gross Amount shows zero or incorrect value
docs.text: Symptom: The scheme header shows zero or outdated annual amounts even though lines have correct values.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: The Annual Gross Amount is a calculated field (FlowField) that may not refresh automatically in certain navigation scenarios. Close and reopen the scheme card from Perception Scheme Dates to force recalculation.

docs.title: Process canceled by the user
docs.text:
Error: "Process canceled by the user"

This occurs when a duplicate concept is detected during journal posting and neither Replace nor Add was selected.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
When the duplicate dialog appears, choose one option:

  • Replace: Overwrites the existing value.
  • Add: Accumulates the new amount on top of the existing one.

If neither option is appropriate, remove the duplicate lines from the journal before posting.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Perception Schemes FAQ
  • Register Variable Perceptions
  • Perception Schemes Overview

docs.title: Salary Concepts Overview in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Salary concepts are the master catalog of all compensation elements in the payroll system. Each concept defines tax rules, social security contributions, garnishment behavior, accounting integration, and payroll calculation logic that propagates automatically to perception schemes, labor agreements, and payroll lines.

docs.title: Key facts
docs.text:
• Salary concepts are shared across all companies in Business Central. A change to a concept affects every company that uses it.
  • Each concept is uniquely identified by the combination of Code and Concept Type.
  • Concept types include: Earning (income), Deduction (discount), Bases (calculation base), Text (informational), and Cost (company cost).

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
• Create and configure salary concepts with tax, contribution, and accounting properties.
  • Propagate concept changes to all perception schemes and labor agreements that reference them.
  • Configure benefit-in-kind concepts with linked income-on-account and deduction entries.
  • Set up flexible remuneration concepts with fiscal exemption limits.
  • Configure prorated social security contributions for variable concepts.
  • Mass-update garnishment settings across concepts and historical payroll lines.

docs.title: How concepts flow through the system
docs.text:
1. A salary concept is defined with its structural properties.
  2. The concept is referenced in labor agreement lines (with amounts by category).
  3. When the agreement is applied, lines are transferred to each employee's perception scheme.
  4. During payroll calculation, the concept rules determine how each line is computed.
  5. During posting, the accounting group of the concept defines the ledger accounts to use.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before creating salary concepts, configure:

  • Perception keys (for tax treatment)
  • Contribution types (for additional social security contributions)
  • Concept accounting groups (for ledger integration)
  • Extra pays (for concepts with periodicity longer than one month)

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Set Up Salary Concepts
  • Create an Earning Concept
  • Propagate Concept Changes
  • Salary Concepts Field Reference

docs.title: Configure a Benefit in Kind Concept in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Benefits in kind (company vehicle, medical insurance, meal vouchers) require a specific configuration that links the main concept with income-on-account and in-kind deduction entries.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A perception key of type in-kind defined (for example, ESPECIE).
  • An income-on-account concept already created (Earning type).
  • An in-kind deduction concept already created (Deduction type).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that the auxiliary concepts exist:
  3. An Earning concept for income on account (for example, INGCTA).
  4. A Deduction concept for the in-kind deduction (for example, DVEHEMP).
  5. Create the main concept: set Code to VEHEMP and Concept Type to Earning.
  6. In the Perception Key field, select an in-kind key (for example, ESPECIE). The In Kind field is automatically set to Yes.
  7. Set Income on Account to Yes.
  8. In the Company Income on Account Concept field, select the income concept (for example, INGCTA).
  9. In the In Kind Deduction Concept field, select the deduction concept (for example, DVEHEMP).
  10. Set Subject to Contribution to Yes.
  11. In the Concept Accounting Group field, select the group (for example, INESPECIE).

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The main concept has In Kind inherited as Yes. The auxiliary concepts are correctly linked. When included in a perception scheme, payroll automatically generates the income-on-account and deduction lines.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Configure Flexible Remuneration
  • Create an Earning Concept
  • Set Up Salary Concepts

docs.title: Configure Flexible Remuneration Concepts in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Flexible remuneration concepts (meal vouchers, medical insurance, nursery, etc.) require additional configuration to manage fiscal exemption limits and associated deductions.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A flexible remuneration deduction concept already created (Earning type).
  • An exemption limit defined in AT and EP Contribution Types (if applicable).
  • A suitable perception key (typically in-kind type).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate or create the concept (for example, Code = CHREST, Concept Type = Earning).
  3. Set Flexible Remuneration to Yes.
  4. In the Perception Key field, select the appropriate key. The In Kind and IRPF Exempt values are inherited automatically.
  5. In the Flexible Remuneration Deduction Concept field, select the deduction concept (for example, RDCHREST).
  6. In the Exemption Limit Code field, select the fiscal exemption limit if one exists.
  7. In the Limit Excess Concept field, select the concept that captures the excess over the exemption limit if applicable.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The concept is configured as flexible remuneration with all links correctly set. During payroll, when the amount exceeds the exemption limit, the system automatically generates the excess concept line.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Configure a Benefit in Kind Concept
  • Create an Earning Concept
  • Troubleshooting Salary Concepts

docs.title: Configure Prorated Social Security Contribution in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Some variable concepts do not contribute monthly to social security but instead contribute proportionally when they are earned. This requires a specific configuration with mandatory prerequisites.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The concept must be marked as Variable = Yes.
  • The concept must not have Subject to Contribution = Yes (they are mutually exclusive for prorated contribution).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the concept (for example, COMVEN for sales commissions).
  3. Set Variable to Yes.
  4. Set Subject to Contribution to No.
  5. Set Contribute on Proration to Yes.

docs.title: Important
docs.text: The order matters. The system validates that Variable is Yes and Subject to Contribution is No before allowing you to enable Contribute on Proration. If you do not follow this order, the system displays a validation error.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The concept has prorated contribution active. During payroll, the social security contribution is distributed proportionally to the earning period.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Create an Earning Concept
  • Troubleshooting Salary Concepts
  • FAQ Salary Concepts

docs.title: Create an Earning Concept with Tax and Contribution Settings
docs.text: Use this procedure to add a new compensation element that contributes to social security and has a specific tax treatment. This covers the majority of payroll concepts.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A suitable perception key defined in the Perception Keys master.
  • An existing accounting group (for example, SALARIOS).
  • An additional contribution type if applicable (for example, HEXTRA for overtime).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. Create a new line in the list.
  3. In the Code field, enter a unique identifier, for example PNOCT.
  4. In the Concept Type field, select Earning.
  5. In the Description field, enter a descriptive name, for example Night shift bonus.
  6. Set Subject to Contribution to Yes.
  7. In the Perception Key field, select the appropriate key. The IRPF Exempt and In Kind fields are automatically inherited.
  8. Set Variable to Yes if the amount changes each month.
  9. Set Guaranteed Salary to Yes if the concept is part of the guaranteed salary for sick leave or work accident calculations.
  10. In the Concept Accounting Group field, select the group, for example SALARIOS.
  11. Verify that Garnishable is automatically set to According to SMI (the default for earnings).
  12. Optionally, select a Subconcept value for detailed classification.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The concept line appears in the list with all fields correctly populated. The IRPF Exempt and In Kind values reflect the settings inherited from the perception key. The concept is ready to be used in perception schemes and labor agreements.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Configure a Benefit in Kind Concept
  • Propagate Concept Changes to Schemes
  • Set Up Salary Concepts

docs.title: FAQ for Salary Concepts in Omne RH Payroll
Why can't I edit the IRPF Exempt and In Kind fields directly?
docs.text: These fields are automatically inherited from the Perception Key assigned to the concept. This design ensures that all concepts with the same perception key have consistent fiscal treatment. To change the value, either modify the perception key in the Perception Keys master or assign a different perception key to the concept.

docs.title: What is the difference between Subject to Contribution and Contribute on Proration?
docs.text:
Mode Behavior Typical use Subject to Contribution = Yes The concept contributes to social security every month it appears in payroll Base salary, fixed bonuses, agreement supplements Contribute on Proration = Yes The concept only contributes when it is earned, distributing the contribution proportionally Quarterly commissions, annual bonuses, irregular variable concepts

To enable Contribute on Proration: first set Variable to Yes, then set Subject to Contribution to No, then set Contribute on Proration to Yes. The order is mandatory.

docs.title: What happens when I propagate changes if a scheme has custom conditions?
docs.text: Propagation updates structural fields (Subject to Contribution, Accounting Group, Prorate, Variable, Subconcept, Perception Key, IRPF Exempt, In Kind) but never modifies amounts, formulas, or units/price in the scheme. Individual employee compensation conditions remain intact.

docs.title: Why are earnings automatically set to "According to SMI" for garnishment?
docs.text: This is by design for Earning type concepts. Spanish law establishes that salaries are garnishable according to a scale based on the minimum interprofessional salary (SMI). The system applies this rule as the default. If a concept should not follow this rule (for example, an indemnification), manually set its garnishment to Not Garnishable or Fully.

docs.title: When should I use the Provision field, and what do the values mean?
docs.text:
Value Effect Use case (empty) No provision Regular monthly concepts Variable Provisioned and de-provisioned when earned Extra pays provisioned monthly and settled at payment Without De-provision Provisioned but no de-provision generated Concepts accumulated without periodic settlement

The Extra Pay No. field must be set before configuring the provision.

docs.title: What does "system concept" mean and what are the limitations?
docs.text: System concepts are predefined records that cannot be deleted. If you try to delete one, the system shows: "You can't erase predefined concepts for the system." You can modify their properties (description, accounting group, etc.) but their existence is protected because the payroll engine references them internally.

docs.title: Can the same code exist for different concept types?
docs.text: Yes. The primary key is the combination of Code + Concept Type. A concept SB of type Earning and another SB of type Bases are independent records with different properties. When searching or referencing a concept, the system always filters by type.

docs.title: What is the difference between "Excluded Part Time" and Quantity Management "Excluded Part Time"?
docs.text:
Field Effect Excluded Part Time (field) The concept amount is not prorated proportionally to the part-time contract hours Quantity Management = Excluded Part Time The quantity (units) is not adjusted for part time, but the amount may still vary

Both fields protect the concept from automatic part-time adjustments, but they act on different dimensions (amount vs. quantity).

docs.title: Propagate Concept Changes to Schemes and Agreements
docs.text: When you modify a salary concept property (contribution, accounting group, perception key, etc.), you must propagate the change to all perception schemes and labor agreement lines that reference the concept.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A concept with pending modifications to propagate.
  • Verify the change is correct before propagating, as it affects all employees and agreements.

docs.title: Option A: Automatic confirmation on save
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the concept to modify (for example, PTRANS).
  3. Modify the desired field (for example, set Subject to Contribution to Yes).
  4. When you leave the line, the system displays a confirmation: Do you want to apply the changes?
  5. Choose Yes to propagate to all schemes and agreements automatically.

docs.title: Option B: Manual action
docs.text:
1. Make the modification without confirming the automatic propagation.
  2. Select the modified concept in the list.
  3. Choose the Apply Changes action in the Process group.
  4. The system updates all schemes and agreements that reference the concept.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system displays the number of updated records in schemes and agreements. The propagated fields are: Subject to Contribution, Accounting Group, Prorate, Variable, Subconcept, Perception Key, IRPF Exempt, and In Kind. Amounts, formulas, and units/price are never propagated (they are specific to each scheme or agreement).

docs.title: Important
docs.text:
• If you chose No at the automatic confirmation and did not run Apply Changes, the modifications only exist in the concept master.
  • The propagation updates ALL agreement lines that reference the concept. If an agreement requires different settings, adjust it manually after propagation.

docs.title: Set Up Salary Concepts in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before creating salary concepts, verify that the required master data is configured. Then create concepts with identification, tax, contribution, payroll, and accounting properties.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Requirement Where to verify Perception keys defined Choose the search icon, enter "Perception Keys", and choose the related link Contribution types configured Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Types", and choose the related link Concept accounting groups created Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concept Accounting Group", and choose the related link Extra pays defined Choose the search icon, enter "Company Extra Pays", and choose the related link INEM tables (SS codes) Choose the search icon, enter "INEM Tables", and choose the related link

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. The page is an editable list (there is no separate card page).
  3. Create a new line and fill in the minimum required fields:
  4. Code: Unique identifier (up to 10 characters), for example SB.
  5. Concept Type: Select the nature of the concept: Earning, Deduction, Bases, Text, or Cost.
  6. Description: Descriptive name, for example Base salary.
  7. Set the Subject to Contribution field to Yes if the concept contributes to social security.
  8. Assign a Concept Accounting Group for ledger integration, for example SALARIOS.

docs.title: Configure tax properties
docs.text:
Tax properties are managed through the Perception Key field:

  1. In the concept line, select a value in the Perception Key field.
  2. The system automatically inherits the IRPF Exempt and In Kind values from the perception key master.
  3. These inherited fields are read-only on the concept. To change them, modify the perception key or assign a different one.

docs.title: Configure contribution properties
docs.text:
• Subject to Contribution: Set to Yes for concepts that contribute monthly to social security.
  • Additional Contribution: Specify a contribution type if the concept has a differentiated rate (for example, overtime).
  • Contribute on Proration: For variable concepts that contribute proportionally when earned (requires Variable = Yes and Subject to Contribution = No).

docs.title: Configure payroll behavior
docs.text:
• Subconcept: Detailed classification (INSS benefit, Worker quota, IRPF withholding, etc.).
  • Variable: For concepts whose amount changes each month.
  • Prorate: For concepts prorated by days worked.
  • Periodicity Greater than Month: For concepts such as extra pays.
  • Extra Pay No.: Link to a specific extra pay.
  • Garnishable: Garnishment level (According to SMI, Fully, or Not garnishable).

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
After creating the basic concepts, confirm:

  • Each concept has a code, type, and description.
  • Concepts with special tax treatment have a Perception Key assigned.
  • Contributing concepts have Subject to Contribution = Yes or Additional Contribution specified.
  • Each concept has an accounting group assigned.
  • Text and Cost type concepts do not contribute and are not taxed (informational only).

docs.title: Troubleshooting Salary Concepts in Omne RH Payroll
Cannot delete a salary concept
docs.text:
Symptom: The system shows an error when you try to delete a concept.

Cause: The concept has System Concept = Yes, meaning it is predefined by the application and protected against deletion.

Resolution: System concepts cannot be deleted. If the concept is no longer needed, remove it from the perception schemes and labor agreements that reference it. The concept remains in the catalog.

docs.title: IRPF Exempt or In Kind fields are not editable
docs.text:
Symptom: The fields appear grayed out and do not allow modification.

Cause: Both fields are automatically inherited from the perception key assigned to the concept.

Resolution: - To change the value: modify the perception key in the Perception Keys master page. - To use different settings for this specific concept: assign a different perception key. - If you clear the perception key, both fields are set to No.

docs.title: Error when enabling Contribute on Proration
docs.text:
Symptom: The system displays a validation error when you try to set Contribute on Proration to Yes.

Cause A: The Variable field is not set to Yes.

Cause B: The Subject to Contribution field is still set to Yes.

Resolution: Follow the correct order: 1. Set Variable to Yes. 2. Set Subject to Contribution to No. 3. Set Contribute on Proration to Yes.

docs.title: Concept changes not reflected in perception schemes
docs.text:
Symptom: After modifying a concept property (contribution, accounting group), perception schemes still show the old values.

Cause: The automatic propagation confirmation was declined and the Apply Changes action was not run manually.

Resolution: 1. Select the concept in the list. 2. Choose the Apply Changes action in the Process group. 3. The system updates all schemes and agreements with the propagated fields.

docs.title: Error when configuring provision
docs.text:
Symptom: The system shows an error when selecting a value in the Provision field.

Cause: The Extra Pay No. field is not set. Provision requires an extra pay to be linked.

Resolution: Set the Extra Pay No. field first, then configure the Provision field.

docs.title: Cannot rename a concept with a blank code
docs.text:
Symptom: The system blocks the rename operation and shows an error.

Cause: Renaming a blank code would affect all related records that reference the empty code.

Resolution: Create a new concept with the correct code and manually migrate the references. The blank-code concept cannot be renamed.

docs.title: Garnishment automatically set to "According to SMI"
docs.text:
Symptom: An Earning concept that should not be garnished according to SMI has this setting applied.

Cause: This is the default behavior for Earning type concepts without an explicit garnishment value.

Resolution: Manually set the Garnishable field to Not Garnishable or Fully as needed for concepts with special treatment.

docs.title: Update Garnishment Settings for Salary Concepts in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Use this procedure to mass-update the garnishment field across all salary concepts and optionally propagate the update to historical payroll lines. This is typically used after a regulatory change or data migration.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. Choose the Load Garnishable Field action in the Process group.
  3. The system processes all concepts and sets the garnishment level according to default rules.
  4. To also update historical payroll lines:
  5. Choose the Update Payroll Lines action.
  6. The system updates garnishment settings in existing payroll lines based on the concept master.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
• Earning concepts without a defined garnishment level are set to According to SMI (the legal default).
  • Historical payroll lines reflect the updated garnishment configuration.

docs.title: Important
docs.text: After the mass update, review concepts that require special treatment (Not garnishable or Fully garnishable) and adjust them manually. The default rule applies SMI-based garnishment to all earnings.

docs.title: Sick Leave and Incidents Overview in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The Sick Leave module in Omne RH Payroll centralizes the management of all work interruptions that require communication with Social Security. It handles temporary disability (IT), work accidents, maternity and paternity leave, absenteeism, strikes, and other situations that affect the employment relationship.

docs.title: Key capabilities
docs.text:
• Register and track all types of work interruptions for employees
  • Automatically generate RED system files (FDI) for Social Security communication via SILTRA
  • Create Delta accident reports for work injuries
  • Import Social Security response files (FIE) to update incident status
  • Calculate contribution bases for sick leave periods
  • Manage confirmation reports during extended leaves
  • Handle relapses linked to previous incidents
  • Create bulk incidents for strikes or ERE affecting multiple employees

docs.title: Supported incident types
docs.text:
• Common illness (temporary disability)
  • Non-work accident
  • Work accident (with or without medical leave)
  • Occupational disease
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Absenteeism
  • Paid and unpaid leave
  • Strike
  • Holidays
  • ERE/ERTE (employment regulation)

docs.title: How it integrates with other modules
docs.text:
• Employees: Each incident belongs to an employee. Access incidents from the employee card.
  • Payroll Calculation: Incidents affect salary calculations, benefits, and supplements.
  • Social Security Contributions: Contribution bases are calculated automatically for RED reports.
  • Contracts: Contract type determines how economic data is calculated.
  • Attendance Control: Incidents can be sent to the attendance system to reflect in timesheets.
