docs.title: Create Bulk Incidents for Strike or ERE in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When a strike or ERE affects a group of employees, you can create individual incidents for all of them automatically instead of registering each one manually.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • An incident code configured for the strike or ERE type exists

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. From the action group Process, choose Bulk Incidents.
  3. Configure the incident parameters:
  4. Incident Code: Select the strike or ERE code (for example, HUE).
  5. Start Date: Enter the start date.
  6. End Date: Enter the end date (same day for a single-day strike).
  7. Hours: Enter hours if it is a partial strike (for example, 4 for a half-day strike).
  8. Filter the affected employees by contribution unit, department, or other criteria.
  9. Choose Execute.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system creates one individual incident per active employee matching the filter. The partial leave percentage is calculated automatically based on strike hours divided by the contractual working hours. Employees who already have an open incident in the same period are skipped automatically.

docs.title: Create a Confirmation Report for Sick Leave in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: During an extended sick leave, the physician issues periodic confirmation reports. Each one must be communicated to Social Security.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An open sick leave incident exists for the employee
  • A sick leave report (PB) has already been sent via RED

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the open incident for the employee.
  3. In the Confirmation Report field, enter the confirmation date issued by the physician.
  4. From the action group Siltra, choose Create Confirmation.
  5. The system creates a confirmation report (PC) with data inherited from the original sick leave report.
  6. The confirmation number increments automatically (first confirmation = 1, second = 2, and so on).
  7. Generate the FDI file from RED Data Query and send via SILTRA.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The confirmation report is registered and communicated to Social Security. The next expected medical review date is updated automatically based on the IT process type.

  • Register medical discharge

docs.title: Sick Leave FAQ in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Frequently asked questions about managing sick leave and incidents in Omne RH Payroll.

docs.title: What is the difference between Start Date and Original Start Date?
docs.text: Start Date is the effective start of the incident, which may include the days charged to the company (typically the first 3 days of leave that the company covers). Original Start Date is the date from the physician's sick leave report. In most cases they match, but for work accidents or professional contingencies they may differ.

docs.title: How do I know if an incident has been communicated to Social Security?
docs.text: Check the RED Notification Count field in the incidents list. If the number is greater than zero, at least one RED report has been created for that incident. To see the details of generated reports, choose the RED Data Query action from the Siltra group.

docs.title: Can I modify an incident after generating the FDI file?
docs.text:
Yes, you can modify incident data at any time. However, if the FDI file was already sent through SILTRA, you must generate a new file with the corrections and send it again. Social Security processes the last file received for each incident.

You cannot modify incidents in periods where a payroll has already been calculated. In that case, void the corresponding payroll first.

docs.title: What is a relapse and how is it registered?
docs.text: A relapse occurs when an employee goes on sick leave again for the same cause of a previous incident that was already closed. To register it, create a new incident with the same code, set the Relapse field to Yes, and select the original incident in the Relapse Incident Code field. The system calculates accumulated days automatically.

docs.title: What are economic data in the RED context?
docs.text: Economic data (DE report) is a complementary communication to the sick leave report that includes the employee contribution bases. Social Security may request them to calculate the benefit. Create them from the incidents list using the Siltra group and choosing Create Econ. Data RED.

docs.title: What is the difference between an accident with leave and without leave?
docs.text:
• With leave: The accident causes medical leave. An individual accident report is generated and sent to the mutual via the Delta system. A RED report is also created for Social Security.
  • Without leave: The accident does not require medical leave but must still be registered. These accidents are accumulated in a monthly consolidated report submitted periodically to the mutual.

docs.title: Can I register incidents for multiple employees at once?
docs.text: Yes, use the Bulk Incidents function from the Process action group in the incidents list. This is useful for strikes or ERE affecting multiple employees simultaneously. You can filter by contribution unit or other criteria to select affected employees.

docs.title: What does the Unalterable Values field mean?
docs.text: When you activate Unalterable Values in an incident, the system will not recalculate economic data (contribution bases, days contributed, and so on) in subsequent processes like payroll calculation. Use this when you have manually adjusted values and do not want them overwritten.

docs.title: How do I send incidents to the attendance control system?
docs.text: Select the incident in the list and choose Send to AC from the Attendance Control action group. The incident is transmitted to the attendance control module and reflected automatically in the employee timesheets for the affected period.

docs.title: Generate Sick Leave Incident Reports in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: You can generate printed reports of incidents or RED submissions for review, auditing, or filing purposes.

docs.title: Generate an incident listing
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. From the action group Reports, choose Listing.
  3. Configure filters: date range, contribution unit, incident type.
  4. Choose Generate to produce the report.

docs.title: Generate a RED submissions listing
docs.text:
1. From the incidents list, go to the Siltra group and choose RED Data Query.
  2. From the RED reports list, choose List Submissions.
  3. The system generates a report with all RED communications sent.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A printable report is generated with the filtered incidents or RED submissions.

docs.title: Import a FIE File From Social Security in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Social Security sends FIE response files through SILTRA with confirmations, rejections, or new notifications about previously communicated incidents. Import these files to keep your incident records up to date.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The FIE file has been downloaded from SILTRA
  • Employees referenced in the file exist in the system with their NAF (affiliation number)

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the FIE file import functionality from the incidents list.
  3. Select the FIE file to import.
  4. Choose the processing mode:
Mode Description Recommended use Skip Reads the file without modifying anything Quick inspection Query Validates data and shows errors without modifying Preview before loading Load Creates and modifies incidents based on file content Standard use Create Inc. and load ED Loads data and also creates RED economic data Full processing
  1. Choose OK and wait for the process to complete.
  2. Review the result report:
  3. The system shows a detail of each action performed.
  4. Errors indicate the employee, date, and problem description.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Incidents are created or updated based on the FIE file content. New sick leave reports, discharge dates, and confirmations are reflected in the corresponding employee records.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use the Query mode first to review potential errors before performing the definitive load.
  • If the report shows "payroll already exists in the period," you must void the corresponding payroll before reimporting the file.
  • Confirmation reports do not trigger this error, so you do not need to void payrolls for confirmations alone.

  • Troubleshooting sick leave

docs.title: Register Maternity or Paternity Leave in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee starts maternity or paternity leave for birth, adoption, or foster care, you must register the incident and communicate it to Social Security.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An incident code configured with the Maternity type exists
  • The employee has an active contract and NAF entered

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by the employee or open incidents from the employee card.
  3. Create a new incident:
  4. In Incident Code, select the maternity code (for example, MAT).
  5. In Start Date, enter the leave start date.
  6. In End Date, enter the expected end date (16 weeks for the mother, corresponding weeks for the father).
  7. From the action group Siltra, choose Create Mat./Pat. RED.
  8. The system generates a maternity certificate (ACM) or paternity certificate (ACP) depending on the case.
  9. Open the RED report card and complete the specific fields:
  10. Maternity Rest Type: Select the applicable modality.
  11. End 4th week paternity and Start/End 5th week paternity (paternity only).
  12. Partial leave coefficient (if partial maternity, enter the working percentage).
  13. Generate the FDI file from RED Data Query and send via SILTRA.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The maternity or paternity leave is registered with the correct report type (ACM or ACP) and communicated to Social Security.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Register a sick leave
  • Sick leave overview

docs.title: Register Medical Discharge for a Sick Leave in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee receives medical discharge, you must close the incident and communicate the discharge to Social Security through the RED system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An open incident exists for the employee (no end date)
  • At least one sick leave report (PB) has been sent via RED for that incident

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the open incident for the employee.
  3. In the End Date field, enter the medical discharge date.
  4. From the action group Siltra, choose Create Discharge RED.
  5. The system creates a discharge report (PA) reusing data from the original sick leave report.
  6. Open the RED report card and fill in the Discharge Cause Code field (for example: Cure, Permanent Disability Proposal, or Death).
  7. Generate the FDI file:
  8. From the Siltra group, choose RED Data Query.
  9. Choose Create RED File and send via SILTRA.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The incident now has an end date and the discharge report (PA) has been communicated to Social Security.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Register a sick leave
  • Create a confirmation report
  • Troubleshooting sick leave

docs.title: Register a Relapse of a Previous Sick Leave in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: A relapse occurs when an employee goes on sick leave again for the same medical condition as a previously closed incident. The system links both incidents and carries over accumulated days and contribution bases.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The original sick leave incident is closed (has an end date)
  • The same incident code applies to both the original and the relapse

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Create a new incident:
  3. In Incident Code, select the same code as the original incident (for example, ENF).
  4. In Start Date, enter the relapse start date.
  5. Set the Relapse field to Yes.
  6. In Relapse Incident Code, select the code of the original incident.
  7. The system automatically calculates the Relapse Day (accumulated sick days).
  8. Contribution bases are either copied from the original incident or recalculated depending on the incident code configuration (Relapse Base Calculation field: "Month before relapse" or "Month before original leave").
  9. If needed, from the Siltra group choose Create Sick RED to generate the RED report with the relapse flag.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The new incident is registered as a relapse linked to the original. Accumulated days and contribution bases are calculated according to the configuration.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• If the relapse arrives through a FIE file, the system automatically links it to the original incident.
  • The original incident must be closed (with an end date). You cannot create a relapse from an open incident.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Register a sick leave
  • Register medical discharge

docs.title: Register a Sick Leave and Communicate to RED in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When an employee presents a medical sick leave report for common illness or non-work accident, you must register the incident and send the communication to Social Security through the RED system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The employee has an active contract and NAF (affiliation number) entered
  • An incident code configured for illness exists (for example, ENF)
  • The contribution unit has the contribution account and mutual configured

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by employee or open incidents from the employee card.
  3. Create a new record:
  4. In the Incident Code field, select the illness code (for example, ENF).
  5. In the Start Date field, enter the date from the sick leave report.
  6. Leave the End Date field empty (the leave is still open).
  7. The system automatically fills the incident type and contingency fields.
  8. From the action group Siltra, choose Create Sick RED.
  9. The system creates a sick leave report (PB) with calculated contribution data.
  10. The RED report card opens for review.
  11. Review the RED report data:
  12. Verify the Contingency Code is correct (1 = Common illness).
  13. Verify the Physician Number (enter it if not filled automatically).
  14. Review the contribution data: bases, days contributed.
  15. Check the probable days/months of leave.

docs.title: Register a Work Accident With Medical Leave in Omne RH Payroll

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incidents", and choose the related link.
  2. Create a new incident:
  3. In Incident Code, select the accident code (for example, ACC).

  5. Leave End Date empty (the leave is still open).
  6. From the action group Delta, choose Create Accident.

General section: - Accident Date: Date the accident occurred. - Time of Day: Hour (0-24 format). - Work Hour: Which hour of the work shift (for example, 2 for the second hour). - Accident Description: Detailed description of what happened. - Professional Situation: Select the applicable option. - Was Habitual Work: Yes or No.

Accident location section: - Accident Location: Habitual center, In-journey travel, Commuting, or Other center. - Traffic: Yes or No (if it was a traffic accident).

Accident classification section (select from Social Security tables): - Location Code, Work Type Code - Physical Activity Code and Physical Activity Material Agent - Deviation Code and Deviation Material Agent - Injury Form Code and Injury Causing Material Agent

Medical data section: - Injury Code and Body Part Injured - Injury Severity: Minor, Serious, Very serious, or Death. - Hospitalized: Yes or No. - Healthcare Facility Type: Hospital or Outpatient.

Preventive modality: Mark at least one option (or mark None).

  1. Choose the Validate Data action to confirm all required fields are filled.

docs.title: Set Up Sick Leave and Incidents in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before you can register sick leave or any other work interruption, you must configure the incident codes, contribution rates, and auxiliary tables.

docs.title: Configure incident codes
docs.text:
Incident codes define the types of leave or absence available in the system.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incident Codes", and choose the related link.
  2. Create a new record for each incident type you need:
  3. Enter a Code (for example: ENF, ACC, MAT, HUE).
  4. Enter a Description of the incident type.
  5. Select the Incident category from the dropdown.
  6. Complete the configuration fields based on the type:
Incident type Key fields to configure Illness Special IT situation (if applicable), Contingency code, Benefit code, Company improvement code Accident Contingency code, Benefit code, Company improvement code Maternity Contingency code, Benefit code Absenteeism Deduct salary, Absence cause code Paid leave Absence cause code Unpaid leave Deduct salary = Yes, No worker contribution = Yes Strike Deduct salary = Yes ERE SEPE benefit/subsidy cause code, Deduct ERE benefit

docs.title: Configure accident contribution rates
docs.text:
Contribution rates define the AT/EP (work accident and occupational disease) percentages by economic activity.

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Accident Contribution Rates", and choose the related link.
  2. For each rate, configure:
  3. Code: Internal identifier
  4. Description: Economic activity description
  5. IT: IT contribution rate (percentage with 3 decimals)
  6. IMS: IMS contribution rate (percentage with 3 decimals)
  7. Accident contribution rate: Official Social Security code

For contribution rate 114, you must also set the Secondary rate field. The system calculates types as 30% of the secondary rate, with minimums of 0.63% for IT and 0.36% for IMS.

docs.title: Troubleshooting Sick Leave Issues in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Common problems and solutions when working with the Sick Leave module.

docs.title: Cannot load the FIE file
docs.text:
Symptom: The system shows a message that the FIE file cannot be loaded.

Solution: 1. Verify the file path is correct and the file exists. 2. Confirm the file is not open in another application (SILTRA, text editor). 3. If the file is compressed (.zip), extract it before importing. 4. Open the file in a text editor and verify: - The first line starts with ETI. - The last line starts with ETF. - Intermediate lines start with valid codes (EMP, TRA). 5. Download the file again from SILTRA and retry.

docs.title: Employee from FIE file not found in the system
docs.text:
Symptom: The import report shows "Employee with the indicated NAF not found."

Solution: 1. Open the employee card and verify the affiliation number (NAF) matches exactly (12 characters). 2. If the NAF is incorrect in the system, correct it. 3. If the employee does not exist, register them before importing. 4. For multi-company environments, verify the contribution account (CCC) maps to the correct company.

docs.title: Payroll already exists in the period
docs.text:
Symptom: The import report shows the error "A payroll already exists in this period."

Solution: 1. Identify which payroll exists in the affected period. 2. Void the payroll for the corresponding period. 3. Re-import the FIE file. 4. Recalculate the payroll to reflect the incident changes.

Confirmation reports (PC) do not trigger this error, so you do not need to void payrolls for confirmations.

docs.title: An incident already exists in the same period
docs.text:
Symptom: The system indicates an incident already exists in the same period for the employee.

Solution: 1. Check the existing incidents for the employee. 2. If the previous incident is still open (no end date), close it first with the discharge date. 3. If dates overlap, adjust one of the incidents so they do not overlap.

docs.title: Relapse cannot find the original incident
docs.text:
Symptom: The FIE file reports a relapse but the system cannot find the original incident.

Solution: 1. Review the employee's past incidents. 2. If the original incident was never registered, create it manually with the correct data before importing. 3. Verify the original incident is closed (has an end date). You cannot create a relapse from an open incident.

docs.title: Missing discharge cause code when generating FDI file
docs.text:
Symptom: Error indicating the discharge cause code is missing in a discharge report (PA).

Solution: 1. From Incidents, go to the Siltra group and choose RED Data Query. 2. Locate the discharge report (PA) with the error. 3. Open the report card and fill in the Discharge Cause Code field (for example: Cure, Permanent Disability Proposal). 4. Regenerate the FDI file.

docs.title: Missing required fields in the Delta accident report
docs.text:
Symptom: Validation errors when generating the accident report.

Common missing fields and where to fill them:

Missing field Location Accident date General section of the accident details card Injury causing material agent Accident classification section Physical activity material agent Accident classification section Healthcare facility type Medical data section Injury severity Medical data section Employee phone number Employee card (not the accident card)

Solution: 1. Open the accident details card. 2. Complete all fields indicated by the error. 3. Verify at least one preventive modality is marked (or mark "None"). 4. Choose Validate Data to confirm all required fields are filled. 5. Regenerate the accident report.

docs.title: Incident code not found when importing FIE
docs.text:
Symptom: The import report indicates no incident code exists for the notified contingency.

Solution: 1. Choose the search icon, enter "Incident Codes", and choose the related link. 2. Verify records exist for the necessary types: - At least one code with Incident = Illness (for common contingencies) - At least one code with Incident = Accident (for professional contingencies) - A code with Incident = Maternity (for maternity/paternity benefits) 3. For special IT situations (menstruation, pregnancy interruption, week 39 of gestation), verify codes exist with the corresponding Special IT Situation value. 4. Verify the Contingency Code field is filled in the incident codes.

docs.title: CCC not recognized in multi-company FIE file
docs.text:
Symptom: When importing a FIE file with employees from multiple companies, some are not resolved correctly.

Solution: 1. Verify the contribution unit has the main contribution account (11 digits) correctly entered. 2. Confirm the company is registered in the system configuration. 3. For first imports, the system creates mapping records automatically during processing.

docs.title: When to contact technical support
docs.text: Contact support if: - The FIE file loads but produces systematically incorrect results - Contribution base calculations do not match after verifying payroll data - Internal errors unrelated to missing data appear - Delta report validation keeps failing after completing all required fields - RED reports show as unsent after correctly generating the FDI file

docs.title: Payroll Simulations Overview in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The Simulations module lets HR managers and finance directors project workforce costs under hypothetical scenarios. You can model salary increases, new hires, headcount reductions, and salary concept changes without modifying actual payroll data.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• Scenario: A hypothesis for salary revision, identified by a code, fiscal year, and revision percentage.
  • Scenario lines: Rules that define what happens to each element (labor agreement category, employee, or salary concept) within the scenario.
  • Simulation results: The calculated monthly and annual costs per employee and salary concept after running a scenario.

docs.title: Available actions for scenario lines
docs.text: Action Description Apply Forecast Applies the scenario salary revision percentage Do Not Apply Forecast Keeps values unchanged (salary freeze) Discard Element Excludes the employee or category from the simulation Increment Element Simulates new hires (N copies of a category) Incident Simulates a leave (sick leave, maternity, etc.)

docs.title: General workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a scenario with the target year and revision percentage.
  2. Configure exceptions (new employees, leaves, concept variations).
  3. Run the generation process.
  4. Review projected costs.
  5. Approve, discard, or adjust the scenario.

docs.title: Related modules
docs.text:
• Employees (Payroll): Provides the employee base for calculations.
  • Contracts: Determines which employees are active in the simulated period.
  • Labor Agreements: Provides professional categories and salary tables.
  • Salary Concepts: Breaks down amounts by concept.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Payroll Simulations
Can I have multiple scenarios for the same fiscal year?
docs.text: Yes. You can create as many scenarios as needed for the same year. This is the standard way of working: create several alternatives and compare them before making a decision.

docs.title: Do simulations modify real payroll data?
docs.text: No. Simulations work with completely separate tables. Employee records, contracts, and actual payroll data are never affected. You can create, delete, and regenerate simulations without any impact on regular payroll processes.

docs.title: What happens if I regenerate simulations for a scenario?
docs.text: When you run Create Simulations again, results are recalculated based on the current scenario configuration and active employee data. Previous results are overwritten. If you modified scenario lines after the first run, regenerating updates the amounts to reflect the changes.

docs.title: What is the difference between Salary Revision % and CPI %?
docs.text:
• Salary Revision %: The percentage actually applied to amounts when the action is "Apply Forecast."
  • CPI %: An informational reference field to document the year's consumer price index. It is not applied automatically in calculations.

The percentage that affects amounts is always the Salary Revision %.

docs.title: What is a Starting Scenario used for?
docs.text: Normally, the simulation starts from real payroll data (contracts, perception schemes). If you specify a Starting Scenario, calculations use that other scenario's results as a base instead of the real situation. This is useful for chaining scenarios. For example, first simulate a freeze (FREEZE2027), then create another scenario that starts from FREEZE2027 to add selective raises.

docs.title: How is the cost of a new hire calculated (Increment Element)?
docs.text:
When Increment Element is set with a quantity of 3:

  • Three fictitious employees are created with the salary structure of the specified category.
  • If a Start Date is specified, the cost is prorated from that date to the end of the fiscal year.
  • If a Discard Date is specified, the cost is calculated only up to that date.

For example, 3 new employees from March 1, 2027 means 10 months of cost (March to December).

docs.title: Can I simulate sick leave?
docs.text: Yes. In the employee-level configuration, you can set the action to Incident and select the type (Illness, Accident, Maternity, etc.). Enter a start date and optionally a duration. The calculation considers the cost reduction during the incident period.

docs.title: How do I know if a scenario has been executed?
docs.text: Open the Scenario Card and choose Simulation Overview. If the results page shows lines with amounts, the scenario has been executed. If it is empty, choose Create Simulations first.

docs.title: Can I delete a scenario?
docs.text: Yes. Deleting a scenario from the list also deletes all its configuration lines and simulation results. This action is irreversible. If the scenario has status Approved, consider changing it to Discarded first to maintain traceability.

docs.title: Are scenarios multi-company?
docs.text: Yes. The Create Simulations process supports multi-company. If the company filter is left empty, it calculates only for the current company. If multiple companies are specified, it calculates for all selected companies.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Payroll Simulations Overview
  • Troubleshooting simulations

docs.title: Troubleshoot Payroll Simulations in Omne RH Payroll
Missing calendar error when creating simulations
Symptom
docs.text: When you choose Create Simulations, an error message indicates that the calendar is missing for the fiscal year.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The simulation process requires a payroll calendar for the scenario fiscal year. If the scenario targets 2027 but the calendar only exists through 2026, the calculation cannot determine working days.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll Calendars", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that a calendar exists for the scenario year.
  3. If it does not exist, create the calendar for that year (copy from the previous year and adjust holidays).
  4. Return to the Scenario Card and choose Create Simulations again.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: After running Create Simulations, all cost amounts show 0.00.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text:
• Employees do not have the Calculate Payroll field enabled.
  • No perception schemes are assigned to the employees.
  • The labor agreement specified in the scenario does not have a valid salary table for the scenario date.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. Verify that employees have the Calculate Payroll field enabled on their card.
  2. Check that employees have a perception scheme with salary concepts assigned.
  3. If you specified a labor agreement in the scenario, verify it has a salary table with amounts valid for the scenario date.
  4. Choose Create Simulations again.

docs.title: Comparison column (Forecast Monthly Cost -2) is empty
Symptom
docs.text: In the Simulations page, the second scenario column shows no data.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text:
• The second scenario filters (Fiscal Year Filter 2 and Scenario Filter 2) are not filled in.
  • The second scenario has not been executed and has no results.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. On the Simulations page, fill in Fiscal Year Filter 2 and Scenario Filter 2 with the second scenario data.
  2. If the column is still empty, open the second scenario and verify it has results (choose Simulation Overview).
  3. If it has no results, choose Create Simulations for that scenario.
  4. Return to the comparison page.

docs.title: Copy Scenario gives a duplicate error
Symptom
docs.text: When you choose Copy Scenario, an error indicates that the code already exists.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: A scenario with the code "[OriginalCode]-COPY" already exists. The copy function automatically generates this code.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. Open the Scenario List.
  2. Find the scenario with code "[OriginalCode]-COPY".
  3. Delete it or rename its code.
  4. Run Copy Scenario again.

docs.title: Salary revision percentage not applied to all employees
Symptom
docs.text: Some employees do not reflect the salary revision percentage in the results.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text: The percentage is only applied to employees and categories whose action is Apply Forecast. If a category or employee has a different action (Do Not Apply, Discard, etc.), the raise does not apply.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. Open Scenario Config. Categories and verify that the desired categories have the action Apply Forecast.
  2. Check Scenario Config. Employees for individual exceptions.
  3. Choose Create Simulations again.

docs.text:
• Frequently asked questions
  • Payroll Simulations Overview

docs.title: Social Security Contributions in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text:
The Social Security Contributions module manages the entire contribution cycle: configuring bases and rates, generating CRETA (IDC) files for transmission to Spain's Social Security system (Sistema RED), and validating data against official FAN files.

This module is essential for monthly payroll compliance. Errors in bases, rates, or contribution segments can cause CRETA file rejections and potential sanctions.

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• Contribution base: The amount on which contribution percentages are applied, calculated from monthly pay plus extra pay proration, subject to minimum and maximum limits per contribution group (01 to 11).
  • Contribution rate: The percentage applied to the base to obtain the contribution amount. Rates exist for common contingencies (CC), unemployment (DESEMP), work accidents (AT/EP), FOGASA, professional training (FP), and MEI.
  • Calculation caps: National parameters defining the minimum wage (SMI), IPREM, and AT/EP caps, updated annually.
  • CRETA segment: A unit of information sent to Social Security representing a continuous period for a worker with unchanged conditions (group, contract, special circumstances).
  • IDC file: XML document containing contribution bases and data for all workers in a period, transmitted via Sistema RED.
  • FAN file: Affiliation and Segments file returned by Social Security for validation against internal data.
  • Allowance: Reduction in employer contributions for specific worker categories (young workers, disabled, long-term unemployed).

docs.title: Monthly contribution cycle
docs.text:
1. Calculate all payrolls for the period.
  2. Verify contribution segments are generated correctly.
  3. Validate payroll data against CRETA expectations.
  4. Generate the IDC file (first in validation mode, then definitive).
  5. Transmit the file via Sistema RED.
  6. Download and import the updated FAN file.
  7. Compare internal segments against FAN to detect discrepancies.
  8. Correct any issues and regenerate if needed.

docs.text:
• Set up social security contributions
  • Generate a CRETA file
  • Validate segments against FAN file
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Adjust Minimum Wage Mid-Year in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When the government updates the minimum wage (SMI) with effect from a date within the fiscal year, you must use the extended fields rather than modifying the original values. This ensures payroll recalculations for prior months use the correct values for their period.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Original year configuration already in place.
  • Official publication of the new SMI with its effective date.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Calculation Caps", and choose the related link.
  2. Locate the record for the current year.
  3. Fill in the extended fields:
  4. Extended Date From: The effective date of the new SMI (for example, 07/01/2026).
  5. Extended Monthly SMI: The new monthly minimum wage amount.
  6. Extended Daily SMI: The new daily minimum wage amount.
  7. If the maximum bases also change, choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Bases", and choose the related link.
  8. For each affected group, fill in:
  9. From Date: The effective date of the new values.
  10. Extended Minimum Base: The new minimum base.
  11. Extended Maximum Base: The new maximum base.
  12. If payrolls have already been calculated for periods after the effective date, recalculate them.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: For payroll periods before the effective date, the system uses the original values. From the effective date onward, it automatically applies the extended values. No manual intervention is needed period by period.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Update contribution tables for a new year
  • Set up social security contributions

docs.title: Assign Bulk Allowances in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When multiple employees qualify for the same contribution allowance, the bulk process assigns it to all matching workers simultaneously instead of updating each employee card individually.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Allowance type created in the master allowances table.
  • Employees with active contracts that meet the filter criteria.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Bulk Allowances", and choose the related link.
  2. On the request page, fill in:
  3. Allowance Type: The code of the allowance to assign.
  4. Application Date: The date from which the allowance applies.
  5. Minimum Age / Maximum Age: Age filters if applicable.
  6. Category: The eligible worker category code if applicable.
  7. Review the employee filter on the data tab to confirm the correct workers are included.
  8. Choose OK to execute.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Employee Allowance records are created for all workers matching the criteria. On the next payroll calculation, the special circumstance codes are included in the CRETA segments for all affected workers.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Assign contribution allowances to an employee
  • Generate a CRETA file

docs.title: Assign Contribution Allowances to an Employee in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Certain worker categories are eligible for reductions in social security employer contributions. These allowances are assigned per employee and transmitted to CRETA as special circumstance codes in the contribution segments.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Allowance type created in the master allowances table (with CRETA special circumstance code assigned).
  • The employee meets the eligibility criteria for the allowance category.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the employee card for the relevant worker.
  2. Navigate to the Employee Allowances section.
  3. Create a new record with:
  4. Allowance Code: The code defined in the allowances master table.
  5. Start Date: The contract start date or the date the allowance becomes applicable.
  6. End Date: Start date plus the allowance duration.
  7. Applied %: The reduction percentage (for example, 50%).
  8. Verify that the related contract also has the allowance assigned in the Contract Allowances section.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: On the next payroll calculation, the system includes the allowance special circumstance code in the CRETA segment (for example, B02) and reduces the employer contribution by the specified percentage.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Assign bulk allowances
  • Set up social security contributions
  • Generate a CRETA file

docs.title: Configure Domestic Workers Contributions in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Domestic workers have a special contribution system based on pay brackets. Instead of the standard group minimum and maximum bases, the system applies a fixed contribution base determined by the worker's monthly pay level.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Contribution Bases table configured for the Domestic Workers regime for the current year.
  • Bases by Amount table populated with the official pay brackets.
  • Employee registered with the Domestic Workers regime.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Bases", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that records exist for the Domestic Workers regime for the current year.
  3. Verify the Bases by Amount auxiliary table:
  4. Each bracket defines a "from amount" and an associated fixed base.
  5. Brackets must cover the full range of possible pay levels.
  6. Ensure the employee's card has the correct regime assigned (Domestic Workers).
  7. When payroll is calculated, the system:
  8. Determines the employee's monthly pay for the period.
  9. Finds the corresponding bracket in the Bases by Amount table.
  10. Applies the fixed base from that bracket instead of group minimum/maximum limits.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The payroll shows the fixed contribution base corresponding to the employee's pay bracket, regardless of the standard contribution group bases.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Set up social security contributions
  • Generate a CRETA file

docs.title: FAQ Social Security Contributions in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Answers to common questions about social security contributions, CRETA segments, and related configuration.

docs.title: What is the difference between Contribution Base and AT/EP Base?
docs.text:
The Contribution Base (Common Contingencies base) is calculated from monthly pay plus extra pay proration, with minimum and maximum limits per contribution group. The AT/EP Base (Work Accidents and Professional Illness) starts from the same pay but also includes overtime hours, and uses different national caps from the Calculation Caps table.

Each contribution rate is linked to a specific base through the Application Base field. For example, Common Contingencies (CC) uses the Contribution Base, while AT/EP uses the AT/EP Base.

docs.title: What happens if a contribution rate is missing for a required code?
docs.text:
If the system cannot find a contribution rate for a mandatory code (such as MEI or FOGASA), the corresponding contribution line will not be calculated. The payroll completes without a blocking error, but the contribution lines for that code will be empty. The CRETA file will be incomplete and rejected by Social Security.

To fix this, choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Rates", and create the missing record with the official percentages.

docs.title: Do the extended fields overwrite the original values?
docs.text:
No. Extended fields (Extended Minimum Base, Extended Monthly SMI, etc.) coexist with the original values. The system selects which to use based on the payroll period date:

  • Periods before the extended date: Original values are used.
  • Periods on or after the extended date: Extended values are used.

This allows recalculating payrolls for earlier months without the new values interfering.

docs.title: How does the system determine if a CRETA segment is Internal or SS type?
docs.text:
Internal segments are generated by the payroll calculation in the ERP. SS segments are imported from the Social Security FAN file. Comparing both detects discrepancies:

  • An Internal segment without a FAN match receives status Surplus (possibly an unreported hire).
  • An SS segment without an internal match indicates data that Social Security has but the ERP does not.

docs.title: When should I use a Supplementary vs. Out-of-Term settlement?
docs.text:
Type Code When to use Normal L00 First settlement of the period Supplementary L02, L03 To correct a previously submitted settlement (differences only) Out-of-Term — For periods submitted after the deadline set by Social Security

Use Supplementary when you detect errors after sending L00. Use Out-of-Term when no settlement was filed within the legal deadline.

docs.title: Is the 75% allowance for workers over 62 on sick leave assigned manually?
docs.text:
No. The system calculates it automatically. When a worker over 62 has a common contingencies sick leave incident, the segment calculation detects the condition and automatically assigns the B06 special circumstance code with a 75% allowance. No manual assignment is needed.

For other allowances (B01 young workers, B02 under 30, B03 over 45), manual or bulk assignment is required.

docs.title: Does the Application Base field distinguish between normal and force majeure overtime?
docs.text: Yes. The available values include both Overtime Base (normal overtime) and Non-Structural Overtime Base. This ensures each contribution rate is applied to the correct base, since force majeure overtime has a reduced contribution rate compared to normal overtime.

docs.title: What is the difference between segment period types?
docs.text:
Period Type When used Contracted Normal active work period Holidays Paid untaken holidays (typically after termination or sick leave) Deferred Termination Period after termination where contributions are still due for deferred wages

Changes in period type within the same month generate separate segments.

  • Troubleshooting social security contributions

docs.title: Generate a CRETA File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Each month, after all payrolls are calculated, you must generate the IDC file containing contribution bases and data for all workers. This file is transmitted to Social Security through Sistema RED.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• All payrolls for the period calculated and validated.
  • Contribution tables updated for the fiscal year.
  • CRETA system activated in Payroll Setup (set to Real or Practice).
  • Contribution segments generated automatically during payroll calculation.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "CRETA Bases File", and choose the related link.
  2. On the request page, fill in:
  3. Period From: First day of the period (for example, 01/01/2026).
  4. Period To: Last day of the period (for example, 01/31/2026).
  5. Settlement Type: Select Normal (L00) for the first settlement of the period.
  6. Validate Only Without Sending: Select Yes for the first run.
  7. Choose OK to generate.
  8. Review the validation results:
  9. If no errors are found, run again with Validate Only Without Sending = No to generate the definitive XML file.
  10. If errors are found, correct them before generating the final file.
  11. The system generates an XML file in IDC 1.0 format.
  12. Transmit the file through Sistema RED.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The IDC XML file is generated successfully. Contribution segments change to Sent status. The file is ready for transmission via Sistema RED.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Validate segments against FAN file
  • Generate a supplementary settlement
  • Validate payroll against CRETA

docs.title: Generate a Supplementary Settlement in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: When errors are detected in a settlement already sent to Social Security, you must generate a supplementary settlement (L02 or L03) containing only the differences. Social Security does not allow cancellation of processed settlements.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Original settlement (L00) already sent and processed by Social Security.
  • Corrected data in the system (affected payrolls recalculated).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Correct the source data and recalculate the affected payrolls.
  2. Choose the search icon, enter "CRETA Bases File", and choose the related link.
  3. Fill in the parameters:
  4. Period From and Period To: Same period as the original settlement.
  5. Settlement Type: Select Supplementary (generates L02 or L03).
  6. Set Validate Only Without Sending to Yes for the first run.
  7. If validation passes, generate the definitive file with Validate Only Without Sending = No.
  8. Transmit the file through Sistema RED.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: A supplementary file is generated containing only the differences in contribution bases. Social Security processes the differences and updates the period's contributions.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Generate a CRETA file
  • Validate segments against FAN file

docs.title: Set Up Social Security Contributions in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before processing social security contributions, you must configure the annual tables that define minimum and maximum bases, national calculation caps, contribution rates, and AT/EP tariffs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Company Setup module configured with contribution units (CCC) and CNAE codes.
  • Employees registered with their social security regime and contribution group.
  • Active contracts with contract type and social security occupation codes.
  • Access to the official Social Security tables for the current fiscal year.

docs.title: Configure contribution bases
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Bases", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that records exist for the current fiscal year.
  3. If no records exist, create one for each combination of regime and group (01 to 11):
  4. Regime Code: Social security regime (General, SEA, Domestic Workers, Artists).
  5. Contribution Group: Group 01 to 11 based on professional category.
  6. Year: Current fiscal year.
  7. Contribution M/D: Monthly (groups 01-07) or Daily (groups 08-11).
  8. Minimum Base and Maximum Base: Values from official tables.
  9. Min. Base/Hour Part-Time: Minimum base per hour for part-time contracts.

docs.title: Configure calculation caps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Calculation Caps", and choose the related link.
  2. Create or update a record for the current year with:
  3. Monthly SMI and Daily SMI: Current minimum wage values.
  4. Monthly IPREM and Daily IPREM: Public income indicator values.
  5. Max. Cap AT/EP Over 18 and Min. Cap AT/EP Over 18: AT/EP limits.

docs.title: Configure contribution rates
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Rates", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify records exist for all required codes: CC, DESEMP, FOGASA, FP, MEI, and ATEP.
  3. For each rate, specify:
  4. Employer %: Percentage charged to the employer.
  5. Employee %: Percentage charged to the employee.
  6. Application Base: Which base to apply (Contribution Base, AT/EP Base, Overtime Base).

docs.title: Configure AT/EP tariffs
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "AT/EP Contribution Rates", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that tariffs exist for your company's CNAE code:
  3. Filter by Element = "CNAE Activities".
  4. Locate the CNAE code configured in the company's contribution unit.
  5. Enter the IT % (temporary disability) and IMS % (invalidity, death, survival) percentages.

docs.title: Activate the CRETA system
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll Setup", and choose the related link.
  2. Set the Contribution System field to:
  3. Practice: Generates segments for testing without sending to Social Security.
  4. Real: Generates segments and files for actual submission.

docs.title: Configure allowances (optional)
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Allowances", and choose the related link.
  2. Create records with: allowance code, description, reduction percentage, duration in months, and the CRETA special circumstance code (B01 to B06).

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system is ready to calculate social security contributions. When payroll is calculated, contribution segments are generated automatically based on these tables.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Update contribution tables for a new year
  • Assign contribution allowances to an employee
  • Social security contributions overview

docs.title: Troubleshooting Social Security Contributions in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Common problems and solutions for social security contribution processing.

docs.title: Payroll shows "No contribution bases found"
docs.text: The system cannot find contribution bases for the employee's regime, group, and year combination.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Bases", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by Year = current fiscal year.
  3. Verify that a record exists for the exact combination of:
  4. The employee's Regime Code.
  5. The active contract's Contribution Group.
  6. The payroll period's Year.
  7. If a record is missing, create it with the official values from the BOE.

docs.title: Contribution base below minimum and CRETA rejects it
docs.text: The calculated CC base is less than the group minimum. This can occur with part-time contracts with few hours or mid-month hires/terminations.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. If the contract is part-time: verify that the Min. Base/Hour Part-Time field is filled in for the relevant group in Contribution Bases.
  2. If the contract is full-time with a mid-month start or end: verify the contract dates to ensure the days contributed are correct.
  3. Recalculate the payroll after the correction.

docs.title: Contributions not calculated for a specific code (FOGASA, MEI, etc.)
docs.text: Contribution lines for a specific code appear empty or zero in the payroll.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Rates", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by Year = current year and Regime Code = employee's regime.
  3. Look for the missing Code (CC, DESEMP, FOGASA, FP, MEI, ATEP).
  4. If no record exists, create one with the official percentages and the correct Application Base.
  5. Recalculate the affected payrolls.

docs.title: CRETA segments with Error status after FAN import
docs.text: After importing the FAN file, some segments show Error status, meaning internal data does not match Social Security records.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Compare critical fields between internal segments and FAN data:
  2. NAF (affiliation number), Start Date, End Date, Contribution Group, Contract Type, SS Occupation Code.
  3. Identify which field differs.
  4. Correct the source data:
  5. Wrong group: Update in the employee's contract.
  6. Wrong dates: Review in the Social Security Affiliation module.
  7. Wrong occupation: Update in the contract.
  8. Recalculate the payroll for the period to regenerate segments.
  9. Re-import the FAN file to verify the correction.

docs.title: Segments with Surplus status (exist in ERP but not in Social Security)
docs.text: Internal segments have no match in Social Security data after FAN validation.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Verify whether the employee's hire was communicated to Social Security.
  2. Check the Social Security Affiliation module for pending affiliation actions.
  3. Once the hire is communicated and processed, download an updated FAN file and re-import.
  4. The segments should change to Validated status.

docs.title: CRETA file rejected for XML format
docs.text: The generated IDC file is immediately rejected by Sistema RED without processing.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Verify there are no invalid special characters in worker data (names with non-standard characters).
  2. Verify the CCC (contribution account code) is exactly 11 characters in Company Setup.
  3. Verify the period format is correct (YYYYMM).
  4. Verify the settlement type is valid (L00, L02, or L03).
  5. Regenerate the file after corrections.

docs.title: Allowance assigned but not applied in payroll
docs.text: An allowance is assigned in the employee card but the employer contribution does not reflect the reduction.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Verify the allowance dates cover the payroll period (Start Date is on or before the period and End Date is on or after).
  2. Verify the allowance duration has not expired.
  3. Check for incompatible allowances assigned to the same employee (only one applies).
  4. Verify the Special Circumstance Code (B01-B06) is filled in the allowances master table.
  5. Recalculate the payroll.

docs.title: No contribution segments generated after payroll calculation
docs.text: Payroll calculates but no CRETA segments are created.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payroll Setup", and choose the related link.
  2. Check the Contribution System field.
  3. If set to No, change it to Practice (for testing) or Real (for production).
  4. Recalculate the payrolls for the period. Segments will now be generated.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Social security contributions overview
  • FAQ social security contributions
  • Validate payroll against CRETA

docs.title: Update Contribution Tables for a New Year in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Each year, the government publishes new minimum and maximum contribution bases, rates, and calculation caps. These tables must be updated before calculating the first payroll of the new fiscal year.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Official tables published in the BOE (Official State Gazette) for the new year.
  • Edit access to the payroll configuration tables.
  • Previous year's configuration as reference.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Bases", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by Year = previous year to use as reference.
  3. Create new records for the current year for each Regime and Group combination:
  4. Update Minimum Base and Maximum Base with the new official values.
  5. Update Min. Base/Hour Part-Time for part-time contracts.
  6. Choose the search icon, enter "Calculation Caps", and choose the related link.
  7. Create a new record for the current year and update:
  8. Monthly SMI and Daily SMI with the new minimum wage.
  9. Monthly IPREM and Daily IPREM with the new public income indicator.
  10. AT/EP caps for workers over and under 18 years old.
  11. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Rates", and choose the related link.
  12. Filter by previous year, copy the records, and update any modified percentages (for example, MEI rate changes).
  13. Choose the search icon, enter "AT/EP Contribution Rates", and choose the related link.
  14. If CNAE tariffs changed, add new records with the updated Application Date.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: When payroll is calculated for the new fiscal year, the system applies the correct bases, rates, and caps. The contribution segments reflect the updated values.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Adjust minimum wage mid-year
  • Set up social security contributions
  • Generate a CRETA file

docs.title: Validate Segments Against FAN File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: After sending the IDC file, Social Security returns a FAN (Affiliation and Segments) file containing the segments as they appear in the official records. Importing and comparing this file detects discrepancies before they result in rejections.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• FAN file downloaded from Sistema RED.
  • Internal contribution segments generated (status Sent or Prepared).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Download the FAN file from Sistema RED.
  2. Choose the search icon, enter "Receive CRETA Files", and choose the related link.
  3. Select the downloaded FAN file.
  4. The system imports Social Security segments and compares them automatically:
  5. Matching segments receive status Validated.
  6. Internal segments without a match in Social Security receive status Surplus.
  7. Social Security segments without an internal match are imported as type SS.
  8. Segments with discrepant data receive status Error.
  9. Review segments with Surplus or Error status:
  10. Choose the search icon, enter "Contribution Segments", and choose the related link.
  11. Filter by status to locate discrepancies.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: All internal segments have status Validated. Any discrepancies are clearly marked for correction before the next submission.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Generate a CRETA file
  • Generate a supplementary settlement
  • Troubleshooting social security contributions

docs.title: Validate Payroll Against CRETA in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before generating the definitive IDC file, run the CRETA payroll validation to compare internal contribution calculations with what Social Security expects. This detects discrepancies before submission, avoiding rejections and supplementary settlements.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Payrolls for the period calculated.
  • Contribution segments generated.
  • Updated FAN file imported (recommended but optional).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Validate CRETA Payroll", and choose the related link.
  2. Filter by the period to validate.
  3. Run the report.
  4. Review the results:
  5. Calculated bases vs. expected: Differences in CC, CP, and overtime bases.
  6. Generated segments vs. FAN: Discrepancies in dates, groups, or special circumstances.
  7. Calculated contributions vs. Social Security: Differences in contribution amounts.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The report confirms that all bases, segments, and contributions match expected values. No significant differences are found, and the IDC file can be generated with confidence.

docs.title: If differences are found
docs.text:
• Base differences: Review which salary concepts contribute to the base and verify extra pay proration.
  • Segment differences: Review contracts, start/end dates, and contribution group.
  • Special circumstance differences: Review sick leave incidents, allowances, and part-time status.

After correcting the source data, recalculate the affected payrolls and run the validation again.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Generate a CRETA file
  • Validate segments against FAN file
  • Troubleshooting social security contributions

docs.title: Social Security Files in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The Social Security Files module manages all electronic communication between your company and the Spanish Social Security system (TGSS — Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social). It centralizes the generation, submission, reception, and validation of regulatory files required for contribution, affiliation, and employment regulation obligations.

docs.title: Key capabilities
docs.text:
• Generate TC2 files with employee contribution bases and quotas
  • Generate CRA files with salary concept breakdowns for TGSS
  • Request and receive CRETA files for contribution segment management
  • Generate RED affiliation files in batch
  • Create ERTE/ERE certificates for employment regulation proceedings
  • Submit FLC forms for workplace accident and occupational illness declarations
  • Validate payroll data against TGSS calculations
  • Notify working days for agricultural or unpaid internship workers

docs.text: System Purpose RED Electronic communication for affiliation and compensation data (AFI, CRA, TC2) CRETA Contribution segment and base management SILTRA Direct quota liquidation (TC2, working day notifications, RNT) FLC Electronic form for accident and illness declarations Certifica2 Employment regulation certificates (ERTE/ERE)

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Calculate and post payrolls for the period.
  2. Generate the required file (TC2, CRA, CRETA bases).
  3. Submit the file to TGSS through the corresponding system.
  4. Receive the response from TGSS.
  5. Validate returned data against internal records.
  6. Correct discrepancies if any and resubmit.

docs.title: FAQ for Social Security Files in Omne RH Payroll
When should I generate the TC2 file?
docs.text: Generate the TC2 file after the monthly payroll closing. It must be submitted before the TGSS deadline, which is typically the last business day of the month following the contribution period. Ensure all payrolls for the period are calculated and posted before running the process.

docs.title: What is the difference between the CRA file and the CRA concepts list?
docs.text:
Both use the same data (salary concepts with SS codes). The difference:

  • CRA File RED System: Generates the final file for submission to TGSS.
  • CRA Concepts List: Generates a review report to verify data before submission.

Always run the list report first to detect potential errors.

docs.title: Can I generate files for multiple companies at once?
docs.text: Yes. The processes iterate automatically across all configured companies. If you leave the Name filter empty, the process generates files for all companies. Use the Name filter to limit to a specific company.

docs.title: What do the CRETA validation error codes mean?
docs.text: Code Meaning I001 Segment does not exist in the system (must be created) I002 Contribution unit (CCC) does not match I003 Contract code is different I004 Contribution group does not match I005 Occupation code is different I006 Part-time percentage does not match I009 Segment end date is different

docs.title: What is an FIE file and when should I process it?
docs.text: FIE files are electronic signature files that may accompany CRETA responses. Process them by selecting the Process FIE Files option in Receive CRETA Files. Only enable this when you receive files with an electronic signature component.

docs.title: Can I generate a partial ERTE certificate for specific employees?
docs.text: Yes. Use the Employee No. filter in the ERTE/ERE certificate reports to limit the certificate to specific employees. This is useful for resending individual certificates or processing partial registrations.

docs.title: Why does a salary concept not appear in the CRA file?
docs.text: The concept does not have the SS Code field filled. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and verify the SS Code. Concepts without this code have no Social Security classification and are excluded from the CRA file.

docs.title: How do I know if an affiliation record was already sent?
docs.text:
Choose the search icon, enter "Affiliation", and check:

  • Sent Date: If filled, the record was included in a previous AFI file.
  • Sent Time: Submission time.
  • Sent User: User who ran the process.

Records with these fields empty are still pending.

docs.title: What happens if I generate TC2 twice for the same period?
docs.text: The system deletes existing TC2 headers and lines for the same combination of unit, period, regime, and type before generating new ones. The TC2 is completely regenerated. No duplicates accumulate.

docs.title: How does the multi-period option work?
docs.text:
Multi-period processes iterate month by month within the specified range (Multi-period Start to Multi-period End). This is useful for:

  • Arrears liquidations covering several months.
  • Quarterly regularizations.
  • Batch submissions of accumulated periods.

docs.title: Generate RED Affiliation File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Use the batch affiliation file process to send employee registrations (altas), terminations (bajas), or changes (variaciones) to TGSS through the RED system in a single file.

docs.title: Prerequisites

docs.title: Steps

1. Choose the search icon, enter "Affiliation File R.E.D Batches", and choose the related link.

  3. Name: Select the company.
  4. Send Date: Enter the planned submission date.
  5. Optionally filter by Last Modified Date or Modified User.
  6. Choose OK to generate the file.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system generates the .AFI or .CFA file with all pending affiliation records matching the filters. Processed records are automatically updated with the submission date and time. Upload the generated file to the RED system.

docs.title: How to check if a record was already sent
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Affiliation", and choose the related link.
  2. Review the following fields:
  3. Sent Date: If filled, the record was already included in a previous file.
  4. Sent Time: Submission time.
  5. Sent User: User who ran the process.

Records with these fields empty are still pending submission.

docs.title: Generate CRA File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The CRA file (Comunicación de Retribuciones Abonadas) communicates the salary concepts paid to employees during a period, classified by Social Security code. Generate this file to submit through the RED system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Payrolls for the period must be calculated and posted.
  • Salary concepts must have the SS Code field configured with the Social Security classification code.
  • Concepts without an SS Code are excluded from the file.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "CRA File RED System", and choose the related link.
  2. On the request page, set the filters:
  3. Concept Code / SS Code: Filter by specific concepts if needed.
  4. Name: Select the company.
  5. Contribution Regime: Select the regime.
  6. Unit No.: Select contribution unit(s).
  7. Operation Type: Select the liquidation type.
  8. Posting Date: Enter the payroll period range.
  9. Choose OK to generate the file.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system groups amounts by Social Security concept code and generates the CRA file for submission to TGSS through the RED system.

docs.title: Review data before generating
docs.text:
Before creating the final file, run the CRA Concepts List report to review the data:

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "CRA Concepts List", and choose the related link.
  2. Use the same filters as for the CRA file.
  3. Review the report for unexpected values or missing concepts.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:

docs.title: Generate CRETA Bases File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Generate the contribution bases file to submit to TGSS through the CRETA system. The file contains calculated bases per contribution segment, including sick leave and special period adjustments.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• CRETA segments must be validated (no segments in "Error" status).
  • Payrolls must be calculated and posted for the period.
  • Employees must have a valid Social Security Affiliation Number (NAF).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "CRETA Bases File", and choose the related link.
  2. On the request page, set the filters:
  3. Name: Select the company.
  4. Contribution Regime: Select the regime.
  5. Unit No.: Select contribution unit(s).
  6. Affiliation No.: Optionally filter by a specific NAF.
  7. Employee No.: Optionally filter by a specific employee.
  8. Choose OK to generate the XML bases file.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system calculates contribution bases per segment, including any sick leave (IT/AT) adjustments, and generates the XML file. Upload the file to the TGSS CRETA system.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• If no payrolls exist for the segment period, the bases will be empty and the employee will be excluded.

The system collects ERE-type incidents, illness, accident, maternity, and vacation records for the selected employees.

1. Choose the search icon, enter "Certifica2 Prior Transmission", and choose the related link.

Use the corresponding list reports to verify data before sending:

docs.title: Generate TC2 File in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: The TC2 file contains the nominal list of employees with their contribution bases and social security quotas. Generate it after the monthly payroll closing to submit to TGSS through SILTRA.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Payrolls for the period must be calculated and posted.
  • Employees must be assigned to contribution units with an active contribution regime.
  • The Excluded from Contribution field must be unmarked on payroll headers.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Payrolls R.E.D. - TC2", and choose the related link.
  2. On the request page, set the filters:
  3. Name: Select the company.
  4. Contribution Regime: Select the regime (for example, "0111").
  5. Contribution Unit No.: Select the unit (for example, "UC001").
  6. Posting Date: Enter the period range (for example, 01/06/2025..30/06/2025).
  7. Choose OK to run the process.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system generates the TC2 file including all active employees in the selected contribution unit for the specified period. Upload the generated file to SILTRA for submission to TGSS.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• If you run the process again for the same unit, period, regime, and type combination, the system replaces the previous TC2 data completely. No duplicates are created.
  • If you do not set the Name filter, the process generates files for all configured companies.
  • Use the multi-period option (Multi-period Start and Multi-period End) to cover several months in a single run.

docs.title: Receive CRETA Files in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: After requesting files from TGSS, you receive responses containing employee data, contribution segments, calculations, and declarations. Load these files into the system for validation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A CRETA request must have been submitted previously.
  • Response files must be available in the configured SILTRA directory.
  • The telematic site must be configured with the correct directory path.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Receive CRETA Files", and choose the related link.
  2. On the request page, set the fields:
  3. File Load Type: Select the file type to load (Response, TyT, DCL, RLC, RNT, Calculations, FIE).
  4. Process FIE Files: Select if there are pending electronic signature files.
  5. Site Code: Select the configured SILTRA telematic site.
  6. Directory Path: Enter the folder path where the received files are located.

The system processes each file according to its type:

  • TyT files: Loads employees and contribution segments.
  • Response files: Processes errors and confirmations.
  • DCL files: Loads calculation declarations.
  • RNT files: Loads the Nominal Workers List.

Review the results after loading to check for errors.

docs.title: Set Up Social Security Files in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Before generating social security files, you must configure master data, telematic sites, and verify that payrolls are correctly calculated and posted.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Companies must be configured with tax ID (CIF) and contribution account codes (CCC).
  • Employees must have a Social Security Affiliation Number (NAF) assigned.
  • Contribution units must be created and assigned to employees.
  • Active contribution regimes must exist with the No Contribution field unmarked.
  • Payrolls for the period must be calculated and posted.

docs.title: Step 1: Verify company setup
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Company Setup", and choose the related link.
  2. For each company, verify the following fields are filled:
  3. Name: Company name
  4. CIF: Tax identification code
  5. CCC: Social Security contribution account(s)
  6. Choose Save.

docs.title: Step 2: Verify contribution regimes
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Regime Control", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that active regimes have:
  3. Contribution Regime: The regime code (for example, 0111 for General Regime)
  4. No Contribution: Unmarked (must be FALSE for the regime to generate files)
  5. Choose Save.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure telematic sites
docs.text:
For systems requiring electronic communication (CRETA, SILTRA, FLC):

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Telematic Sites", and choose the related link.
  2. For each site, configure:
  3. Site Code: System identifier (for example, SILTRA, CRETA, FLC)
  4. Directory Path: Folder path for sending and receiving files
  5. Credentials: API Key or certificates as required by the system
  6. Choose Save.

docs.title: Step 4: Verify salary concepts for CRA
docs.text:
If you plan to generate CRA files (Compensation Paid Communication):

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Salary Concepts", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that each concept has the SS Code field filled with the Social Security classification code.
  3. Concepts without an SS Code are excluded from the CRA file.

docs.title: Step 5: Configure affiliation for RED files
docs.text:
If you plan to generate RED affiliation files:

  1. Choose the search icon, enter "Affiliation", and choose the related link.
  2. Verify that records pending submission have:
  3. Send Date: Planned submission date
  4. Order No.: Record order number
  5. Records that already have a Sent Date value are excluded (already submitted).

docs.text: # Verification 1 Companies configured with CIF and CCC 2 Contribution regimes active (No Contribution = FALSE) 3 Contribution units assigned to employees 4 Telematic sites configured (if applicable) 5 Salary concepts with SS Code (if using CRA) 6 Payrolls calculated and posted for the period 7 User permissions in OMNEPayroll area

docs.title: Submit FLC Form in Omne RH Payroll
docs.text: Use the FLC form process to electronically declare workplace accidents or occupational illnesses to TGSS. The system calculates the sum of AT/EP bases from TC2 headers and submits the data to the FLC service.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The FLC telematic site must be configured with a valid API Key.
  • TC2 data must exist for the contribution unit and period.
  • The contribution unit must have complete identification data (CCC, CIF).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Choose the search icon, enter "Fill FLC Document", and choose the related link.
  2. On the request page, set the fields:
  3. Unit No.: Select the contribution unit of the affected employee.
  4. Late Payment: Select if this is a late payment declaration.
  5. AT/EP Base Rate Type: The percentage applied to the accident/illness base (loaded automatically from contribution rate configuration).
  6. Surcharge Percentage: Enter the applicable surcharge (0-100%), if any.
  7. Period Start / Period End: Enter the declaration period.
  8. Filter by Type: Select to filter TC2 headers by a specific type.
  9. Type: Select Monthly, Complementary, Vacations, or Samples (only enabled when Filter by Type is selected).
  10. Choose OK to submit the form.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The system calculates the sum of AT/EP bases from all TC2 headers for the period and submits the data to the FLC service. A PDF document (FLC.pdf) is automatically downloaded with the result.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
• If you receive a connection error, verify the telematic site configuration and API Key validity.
  • Ensure the contribution unit has all required identification fields filled.
